data:
Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine. Your marketing agency in an app. A small business loses its week to working out what to post, where and for whom, then writing it, posting it, answering comments, chasing leads, and checking whether any of it worked. PULSE does that work, and you approve what goes out.
You give it your website. A check-up reads your site and the web and shows, on Brand Analysis, how your business looks online: your site score, whether AI answers and Google name you, your competitors, partners and leads. From that, PULSE proposes a plan and campaigns, writes the posts for your approval, finds leads and public tenders, posts what you approve at your best times, and shows what came of it.
PULSE shows only figures it actually measured. A number it could not obtain reads Not measured, never 0 and never an estimate. Every AI step runs on your PULSE’s own model server; PULSE calls no outside AI service.
Getting startedSign in and run your first check-up. User guideBrand Analysis, Leads, Campaigns, Studio, Opportunities, results, Integrations: one page per step. How PULSE worksMeasured and not measured, the plan gate, approval and publishing, personas. Brand and connectionsBusiness profile and the administrator’s side of each connection. Admin guideDeployment, configuration, users, publishing switches, billing, and the site pipeline. Developer guideBuild, test, regenerate protos, and call the gRPC API. API referenceEvery gRPC service and method, derived from the .proto files. Agent model cardsWhat each AI agent does, reads, and produces, and where it stops. TroubleshootingReal messages and what to do about each one.

data:
Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine keeps a marketing team’s daily work moving; this guide is for the people who deploy and operate a PULSE instance.
Switches and arming orderEvery publishing, audit-apply, calling, and sign-in switch with its default, and the safe order to turn them on. Configuration referenceEvery environment variable the backend reads, grouped by purpose. Connector setupWhat to configure in the Meta, Google and LinkedIn consoles, GitHub, email and voice. Users and accessBreak-glass admin, Google sign-in, seeded roles, and where Admin lives. Publishing controlsThe kill switch and per-channel arming for everything outward-facing. Site pipelineBlog posts to your site, the daily site audit, and audit-fix pull requests. BillingThe shared Billing page, fed by the operator’s subscription variables and PULSE’s usage ledger. PlansLite, Dedicated, and Enterprise; seat prices, the Lite daily task limit, currency and billing periods. Telephony and messagingAsterisk cold calls, browser voice, and the WhatsApp/SMS edge. OperationsHealth, self-healing, TLS, logging, rate limits, and the licence gate.
data.architecture#Architecture: Part What it is Backend One Go server (pulse-server serve). gRPC, gRPC-Web for browsers, and a few plain HTTP routes share one port. App Flutter, built for the web (served by the backend itself when PULSE_WEB_DIR is set) and for Android. Database SQLite, in the pod, with one writer, so there is one backend instance per deployment. Litestream replicates it continuously to the cluster’s own object store (objectd). There is no other database. Files PULSE’s appfs root on objectd: sessions, sealed media and the memo cache. The server refuses to start if it cannot mount it. Text model The platform’s own inference: PULSE calls the model router (INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL), which sends each request to a tier served by Distro-built mistral.rs on the GX10 inference servers. No third-party model or API is ever called. Product facts Read straight from the files in grpc/data/corpus by search and file reads (direct corpus interaction). There is no embedding step, no vector index and no RAG. Speech Text-to-speech through TIDE’s shared ttsd (TTSD_URL); speech-to-text through the voice tier (VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL). PULSE embeds no speech engine. Secrets OAuth tokens and passwords are sealed with the envelope key TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK before they reach the database. There is no image-generation tier: PULSE draws carousel slides and video frames itself in Go and assembles video with ffmpeg.
data.first-things-to-set#First things to set: Setting Why PULSE_JWT_SECRET Required. The server will not start without it. TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK Required. The database refuses to open without it, rather than write tokens in plaintext. TENANT_ID Names the tenant for billing, the profile page and the Admin page. PULSE_WEB_DIR or CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Serve the app same-origin, or pin the origins that may call the API. INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL, INFERENCE_MODEL The model router, and the model name requests carry. PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL The https address people use. Needed by every sign-in connection, Instagram media and the podcast feed. See Public address and redirects. Then work through Switches and arming order. The full list is in the configuration reference.
data.how-a-change-reaches-production#How a ch:
cd-backend.yml builds the image on every push to main, and again every night at 05:23 UTC (the shared org-runink/ui components are compiled into the image, and its path filter cannot see them). It then compares the digest it pushed with the digest the pod runs and rolls only when they differ (or when it cannot tell): it deletes the pod by its label and waits on deploy/pulse. A pod delete changes no pod template, so the operator has nothing to undo, and imagePullPolicy: Always makes the new pod pull the new image.
Which commit is running is stamped on the live PulseControlPlane, not on the image (werf tags it :latest) or the pods (the operator rewrites their labels):
kubectl -n pulse-system get pulsecontrolplane pulse -o yaml | grep 'runink.org/' runink.org/commit, runink.org/image-digest, and runink.org/rolled-at, rolled-by, rolled-on. rolled-at is written only on success, so its age is the staleness signal: more than about 36 hours means the runs are failing or the schedule stopped. When you compare digests, read the container named backend.
data.what-this-repository-ships#What this rep:
The backend image, built from grpc/Dockerfile with the repository root as the build context. The build is self-contained: it builds the Flutter web bundle (CanvasKit bundled locally, no source maps), clones the sibling libraries grpc/go.mod points at at pinned commits, and compiles a static, cgo-free Go server. Every base image is pinned by digest and comes through a registry build argument (BASE_REGISTRY, FLUTTER_SDK_REGISTRY); see Image build arguments.
The runtime image is debian:bookworm-slim with ffmpeg (Reels, Stories and other videos), chromium (everything that reads live web pages: the audit, lead prospecting, market signals), and Litestream, pinned by SHA-256. The entrypoint restores the database with Litestream, then runs the server under continuous replication.
data.who-deploys-pulse#Who deploys PULSE:
Runink TIDE does. This repository holds application code and the backend image build. Cluster bring-up, the operator and deploys live in TIDE:
# in TIDE's repository, from its grpc/ module go run ./cmd/tide deploy pulse TIDE’s pulse-operator reconciles the instance into the pulse-system namespace from a PulseControlPlane resource. That resource is the authoritative pod spec: change it or its overlay, never the live Deployment, which the operator puts back. TIDE’s k0s overlay sets PULSE_ENV=production.
The names on the cluster:
Object Name Deployment (named after the PulseControlPlane) pulse, so kubectl -n pulse-system rollout status deploy/pulse Pod label app.kubernetes.io/name=pulse-backend Container backend Image pulse-backend, built by this repository’s cd-backend.yml There is no deploy/pulse-backend.

data: Billing (/billing) is the shared Runink Billing page from org-runink/ui. It is its own destination, beside Account and never under it: plan, seats, usage and purchases live here and nowhere else, and the Account page shows none of them. PULSE serves its API, runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService, over the org-runink/billing library, with PULSE-specific hooks. The page lists and prices PULSE’s own plans, never another product’s. For the plans, prices, and the Lite daily task limit, see Plans.
data.several-purchasers-on-one-instance#Sever: On an instance shared by several customers, RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE (the member-to-purchaser file TIDE’s operator projects) maps each signed-in person to the purchaser who pays for their seat. A purchaser’s own row sets their plan and seats, so a Lite purchaser’s seats get the daily task limit and a Dedicated or Enterprise purchaser’s do not. People with no row fall back to the instance’s SUBSCRIPTION_* variables.
data.what-each-part-of-the-page-does#What eac: Feature In PULSE Plan catalog and price quotes (ListPlans, QuotePlan) Work. Pricing is arithmetic, done on the server, from PULSE’s catalogue. Overview of your subscription (GetOverview) Works, from the variables above. Today On Lite, “Today: X of 10 fast tasks” for the viewer’s seat, and the reset time once the limit is reached. Dedicated and Enterprise show no daily count. Estimate Every line is either computed or says why it cannot be. Currency The page shows US-dollar list prices and says so. Invoices are in your regional currency; see Currency and billing periods. Checkout and the billing portal (StartCheckout, OpenPortal) Subscriptions are bought through Runink, so both answer “not configured” and nothing on this page can charge. Seats (ListSeats, AssignSeat, RevokeSeat) Seats come from the subscription; the page shows no seats section. Billing actions are logged to the process log as billing audit lines.
data.where-the-daily-task-count-is-kept#Where: The Lite daily task count lives in the usage bucket TIDE’s operator gives the pod (RUNINK_USAGE_*), as append-only records. When a deployment has no usage bucket, as in local development, tasks are not counted and the page says that daily usage is not tracked on this deployment.
data.where-the-subscription-comes-from#Where:
PULSE runs one deployment per tenant. The subscription is read from environment variables that Runink TIDE’s operator projects onto the pod:
Variable Meaning When missing TENANT_ID The tenant No subscription on record SUBSCRIPTION_TIER The plan tier: lite, dedicated, or enterprise lite SUBSCRIPTION_SEATS Number of seats 1 SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS Subscription status active SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_END End of the current billing period (RFC 3339) No period shown SUBSCRIPTION_ANNUAL true for a yearly subscription Month-to-month The tier, seat, and status defaults apply only when TENANT_ID is set. Without TENANT_ID, the page shows that no subscription is on record. It does not invent a Lite plan. A subscription whose SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS is not active, trialing, or past due grants nothing: it is shown as suspended, never degraded to a free tier.
The page derives the current period from SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_END, running from your subscription’s anniversary date. With no period on record, it shows no period and prices the month-to-month rate. A Dedicated plan is sold yearly only.

data: PULSE is configured through environment variables. This page lists the ones the backend reads, grouped by purpose. It names variables and describes their effect. It does not show values: secrets come from the secret store, and Runink TIDE’s operator projects the rest.
data.billing-and-tenancy#Billing and tenancy: Variable Effect TENANT_ID This deployment’s tenant. SUBSCRIPTION_TIER, SUBSCRIPTION_SEATS, SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS The subscription the Billing page shows. SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_END, SUBSCRIPTION_ANNUAL The current billing period’s end (RFC 3339) and whether the subscription is yearly. RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE The member-to-purchaser file TIDE’s operator projects. Each signed-in person’s plan and seats come from the purchaser it names. RUNINK_USAGE_* The usage bucket TIDE’s operator gives the pod. It holds the Lite daily task count. TIDE_ROUTER_BILLING_KEY_FILE, TIDE_ROUTER_BILLING_KID The service key file and key id PULSE signs its model-router billing claim with. Unset, model calls carry no claim and the router treats them as spot work. Usage is kept on the object store configured under Storage. See Billing and Plans.
data.command-line#Command line: Command Meaning pulse-server serve Starts the backend. --port, -p The port to listen on. Defaults to PORT when set, otherwise 0, which picks a free port.
data.connections#Connections:
Each person connects their own accounts under Settings › Integrations. These are the instance’s app clients that make one-click sign-in possible; all are secrets from the instance’s secret store.
Variable Effect META_APP_ID, META_APP_SECRET Connect with Instagram. See Meta. LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET Connect with LinkedIn. See LinkedIn. LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES true once LinkedIn approved the Community Management API: offers company pages. MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID Connect Microsoft 365 (tenant default common). See Email. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET (under Sign-in) serve YouTube, Search Console and Gmail too.
data.inference#Inference: Variable Effect INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL Use the shared inference plane at this address. Unset means PULSE starts its own mistralrs-server. INFERENCE_MODEL The model name PULSE asks the inference plane for. Unset, it uses the code default, Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M.gguf, which is also the platform inference library’s own default, so a locally managed engine loads the model PULSE then requests. In a cluster the name is only a label: the model router rewrites a general-tier request to the tier’s model. INFERENCE_API_KEY Key for the inference server. INFERENCE_HOST, INFERENCE_IP, INFERENCE_PORT, MISTRAL_PORT Where a local inference child listens. BINARY_MISTRALRS_SERVER, MODEL_DIR, PULSE_AGENT_CONFIG The local engine binary, the model directory, and the agent config (default ./agents/pulse.ini). VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL The speech-to-text server. MODEL_VISION, VISION_REMOTE_URL The vision tier that describes photos and video frames attached to an audit: the model id sent (default vision, which the model router routes to its vision tier; off turns it off) and the plane to send it to (default INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL). Without a remote plane there is no vision tier, and attached photos are marked “image understanding unavailable”. TTSD_URL TIDE’s shared text-to-speech service, as a full URL. Unset means the in-cluster ttsd Service; set to empty turns voice output off. TTSD_CALLER_KEY_FILE The file holding PULSE’s service key for ttsd. Read on every call, so a rotated key needs no restart. INFERENCE_DECODE_TOK_S The platform decode rate that generation budgets are sized from. TIDE injects it. PULSE_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS Wait allowed for the first token. Default 5 minutes. PULSE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Overrides the decode budget outright. PULSE_ADMIT_MAX, PULSE_ADMIT_QUEUE, PULSE_ADMIT_MODE, PULSE_ADMIT_WEIGHTS In-process admission control. Off unless PULSE_ADMIT_MAX is above zero. PULSE_GATE_MAX_INFLIGHT, PULSE_GATE_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS, PULSE_GATE_DECODE_RATE Cross-app admission gate for the shared plane: concurrent submissions (unset means unbounded), the longest acceptable queue wait, and the measured decode rate the wait is sized from. Off unless one is set. PULSE_DEDUP_TTL How long a repeated generation is reused. Go duration, default 1h. PULSE_JUDGEMENT off disables the judging ladder. PULSE_AUDIT_DEADLINE_SECONDS The end-to-end deadline of the diagnostic and the site audit. Default 170, a three-minute budget less the time to render the result. Clamped to 10–900. Every phase’s budget is derived from what is left of it; a phase that does not finish shows on the reasoning card as “not completed within the 3-minute budget” and the result says it is partial. PULSE_BRAIN_MAX_SEQS The brain tier’s --max-seqs. Default 2. Bounds how many judge claims run at once. INFERENCE_PREFILL_TOK_S, INFERENCE_PREFILL_EXPONENT The plane’s prefill curve. The diagnostic trims its prompt to what its phase can prefill. Set from a benchmark of the target hardware. PULSE_RERANKER off ranks the prompt’s context lexically instead of asking the reranker tier (reranker through the model router). PULSE_EGRESS_ALL_AGENTS Widens output screening to every agent. Screened answers arrive whole instead of streaming. PULSE_SKILLS_MODELS A TOML file of per-skill sampling settings, read on top of the built-in models.toml. When set it must be readable and valid, or the server does not start. PULSE_SEARCH_MIN_GAP_MS The least time between two web searches, in milliseconds. Default 2500. TIDE_HEALTH_URL Where agent health reports go. Unset means no reports. See Sovereign inference.
data.media#Media: Variable Effect BINARY_VIDEO_CLI The local video-generation tool behind generated video creatives and course videos (default ./agents/bin/video-gen). Without it those say the tool is not available. Reels and Stories PULSE makes do not use it: they are drawn in Go and assembled with ffmpeg. VIDEO_MODEL_DIR Model directory for video generation. FFMPEG_PATH Overrides the ffmpeg binary. ORPHEUS_BACKEND The compute backend passed to the video tool. Default vulkan.
data.names-that-are-no-longer-read#Names that:
Setting these does nothing. PULSE does not warn about them.
Every LLAMA_* variable, including LLAMA_MODEL and LLAMA_REMOTE_URL. Use INFERENCE_MODEL and INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL. SD_REMOTE_URL. The image-generation tier was retired. TTS_REMOTE_URL. Speech goes to TIDE’s ttsd, at TTSD_URL.
data.publishing#Publishing: Variable Effect PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED The global kill switch. Only the exact value true arms anything. PULSE_PUBLISH_ Narrows one channel: BLOG, PODCAST, AUDIOBOOK, YOUTUBE, INSTAGRAM, SPOTIFY, LINKEDIN, EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS, and the reply keys LINKEDIN_REPLIES, INSTAGRAM_REPLIES, INSTAGRAM_DMS, YOUTUBE_REPLIES. PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS Lets automations do outbound work. Off by default. PULSE_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT Emails one person may send per 24 hours. Default 50. PULSE_OPPORTUNITIES_DISCOVERY The daily read of open procurement data. On by default. PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH, PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON The per-channel arming file, or the same JSON inline. PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS Comma-separated PULSE user ids allowed to publish through the deployment-global channels (LinkedIn, blog, podcast, audiobook). Empty means nobody. PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY Arms the Site Audit’s apply/commit/pr modes, on top of PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true. Off unless an explicit yes. Admins only. PULSE_APPLY_ROOT The only directory an audit-fix repo_path may resolve into. Unset refuses every mode, plan included. PULSE_SITE_REPO, PULSE_SITE_BRANCH, PULSE_SITE_BLOG_DIR, PULSE_SITE_PUBLISH_MODE, PULSE_SITE_AUTHOR, PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL Blog publishing to your website. PULSE_GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, PULSE_GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL The author on commits PULSE makes. YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS public, unlisted, or private. Unset means private. LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN, LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN, LINKEDIN_API_VERSION The deployment’s LinkedIn token (from a secret) and author (person or organization URN), used only for a user with no LinkedIn connection; and the API version header. LINKEDIN_API_BASE Overrides LinkedIn’s API base (tests). PULSE_LINKEDIN_CTA_URL The link the daily LinkedIn draft ends with. Default https://runink.org. PULSE_PODCAST_TITLE, PULSE_PODCAST_DESCRIPTION, PULSE_PODCAST_LANGUAGE Podcast feed metadata. The defaults and the safe order to turn these on are on Switches and arming order. See Publishing controls and Site pipeline.
data.security#Security: Variable Effect PULSE_JWT_SECRET Required. The key that signs and verifies every session. There is no default. It must never be a value that has been committed anywhere. TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK Required. The key that seals OAuth tokens in the database. The database refuses to open without it. SECRET_BACKEND Where secrets are read from. file reads each one from SECRETS_DIR/; any other value reads the process environment. SECRETS_DIR The directory the file backend reads. Default /var/run/secrets. PULSE_TLS_CERT, PULSE_TLS_KEY In-process TLS for direct exposure. Set both or neither. TLS 1.2 minimum, forward-secret AEAD suites only. MESH_MTLS true requires mutual TLS on the listener, with rotating certificates from the shared mesh CA. Takes precedence over PULSE_TLS_*. TLS 1.3 only. MESH_CA_CERT, MESH_CA_KEY The mesh CA, from the secret store. Needed when MESH_MTLS=true. MESH_ISSUER_URL, MESH_ISSUER_TOKEN_FILE The preferred mesh identity: the pod makes its own key and enrols it with TIDE’s mesh issuer, authenticated by the projected ServiceAccount token in the file. MESH_CA_CERT is then only the trust bundle and MESH_CA_KEY is not read. Without MESH_ISSUER_URL, the older shared-CA path (MESH_CA_CERT + MESH_CA_KEY) still works and logs an error on every start. MESH_ADVERTISE_IP, MESH_ADVERTISE_HOST Extra IP and DNS names on the mesh certificate. LICENSE, LICENSE_FILE, LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY An offline licence, inline or as a file, and the key that verifies it. With no licence there is no gating.
data.server#Server: Variable Effect PORT Default for --port. PULSE_WEB_DIR Directory of the Flutter web build. When set, the backend serves the app on the same origin as the API. CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Comma-separated origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Unset means *. Only an exact listed origin gets credentials. PULSE_ENV production (any case) turns the insecure-configuration warnings into a refusal to start. TIDE’s k0s overlay sets it. No billing or plan behavior reads it. See Operations. PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION true turns on gRPC reflection. Off by default. For local work only. PULSE_RATE_RPS, PULSE_RATE_BURST Per-caller rate limit, keyed by peer IP. Off unless PULSE_RATE_RPS is above zero. PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL The public https origin. The base of every sign-in redirect (/oauth/social/callback, /oauth/search-console/callback, /oauth/mail/callback), of the signed /media/ links Instagram fetches, and of absolute podcast-feed links. See Public address and redirects. APP_VERSION The version stamped on log lines. FEATURED_MESSAGES_PATH The file behind the featured-message strip. A2A_ORGANIZATION The organization named on the A2A agent card. Falls back to RUNINK_ORG, then TIDE_GITHUB_ORG, then empty. SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS false (or another no) turns automatic self-healing remediation off; plans are still recorded. Default: on. See Operations.
data.sign-in-and-users#Sign-in and users: Variable Effect PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD (or ADMIN_PASSWORD) Seeds the break-glass admin. Without it, no password login exists. PULSE_ADMIN_USERNAME, PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL Overrides the break-glass admin’s username (admin) and email. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID The Google OAuth client. Without it, Google sign-in is off. OIDC_ISSUER Overrides the token issuer that Google sign-in trusts. AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY true hides the password form. AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS The Google sign-in allowlist. Empty means nobody signs in with Google. AUTH_SEED_USERS Operator-granted roles as email=persona,…. Applied at every start. PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE, PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE The ClientInstance this deployment is. Lets the Admin page write member changes back to it. GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET The Google OAuth client’s secret: Connect with YouTube, Search Console and Gmail, and token refresh. See Google. GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENDPOINT Overrides Google’s token endpoint (tests). See Users and access.
data.site-audit-and-scoring#Site audit and sc: Variable Effect PULSE_SCORING_CONFIG A JSON file overlaid on the built-in scoring config. PULSE_AUDIT_CACHE_TTL How long an audit result is cached, in seconds. Default 3600. PULSE_PROSPECT_AUDIT_TIMEOUT Time limit for auditing one prospect’s site during lead prospecting. Go duration, for example 20s. PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL The site the daily audit engine checks. Falls back to PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL. The engine also needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true before it starts.
data.storage#Storage: Variable Effect PULSE_DB_PATH The SQLite file. Default ./pulse.db. PULSE_DATA_DIR Working data directory. Default ./data. PULSE_APPFS_BUCKET Bucket for the sealed app root (sessions, media, memo cache) on the object store. PULSE_APPFS_DIR Local sealed app root when there is no object store. Default $PULSE_DATA_DIR/appfs. OBJECTSTORE_ENDPOINT, OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET, OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY, OBJECTSTORE_SECRET_KEY The object store for the app root. OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET defaults to pulse-corpus, the bucket the app root has always lived in; do not change it on a running install. LITESTREAM_ENDPOINT, LITESTREAM_BUCKET, LITESTREAM_REGION, LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID, LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Litestream replication of the database. This is a different bucket from the app root’s. When only the LITESTREAM_* variables are set, PULSE fills the OBJECTSTORE_* ones from them at startup, so one object-store configuration serves both. An OBJECTSTORE_* value you set explicitly is never overridden.
data.telephony-and-messaging#Telephony and me: Variable Effect AUDIOSOCKET_ADDR The TCP listener Asterisk streams call audio to. ASTERISK_ARI_URL, ASTERISK_ARI_USER, ASTERISK_ARI_PASSWORD Asterisk’s REST interface, for placing calls. Leave empty to keep outbound calls off. PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS Arms CallLead. Off by default. Callers must also be editor or admin. ASTERISK_ENDPOINT_PATTERN, ASTERISK_CONTEXT, ASTERISK_EXTENSION, ASTERISK_CALLER_ID The dial string, dialplan target, and caller ID. CALLING_AGENT_URL The platform calling agent that carries browser voice calls. PULSE_WEBRTC_SIGNALING_ONLY true answers WebRTC offers locally for signaling tests. Such a call cannot hear the caller. TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN The carrier account behind WhatsApp, SMS and Send / Call. Both are secrets. TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER, TWILIO_VOICE_FROM The WhatsApp sender, the SMS number, and the number calls are placed from. TWILIO_VOICE_FROM is optional and falls back to TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER. PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID Which user’s HubSpot connection backs the WhatsApp sender allowlist, and as whom replies run. PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY true turns automatic WhatsApp/SMS replies on; they also need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP / PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS. Default: off. See Telephony and messaging.

data.audit-pipeline-health#Audit pipeline hea:
Each stage of a one-line audit (Audit a domain) reports to agent health as its own agent, pulse-audit-. Reports go to TIDE_HEALTH_URL; with it unset there are none. A stage that wedges stops reporting, so it shows as stale in the TIDE console rather than idle.
Every run ends with one log line, audit (): . A run is bounded at 45 minutes end to end, and its diagnosis also keeps the PULSE_AUDIT_DEADLINE_SECONDS budget. Time a stage spends waiting for model capacity counts against both.
data.backups-and-the-replica#Backups and the:
In a cluster, Litestream replicates SQLite to the in-cluster object store on the schedule in grpc/litestream.yml. Keep that bucket private to the cluster and treat its credentials like the database’s own.
Once encrypted rows in the new envelope format exist, do not roll back to a build from before that format: it cannot read them.
data.health#Health:
GET /health always answers HTTP 200 with:
{"status":"ok","model_ready":false,"port":8080} The status code is deliberately unconditional. PULSE serves every non-AI feature without a model, so a readiness probe here should catch a wedged or unbound server, not an AI outage. Read model_ready for the model. It is true only when the engine is running and has confirmed it can serve a request.
data.licence-gate#Licence gate: With a licence configured (LICENSE or LICENSE_FILE, verified with LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY), every non-public call is refused with license expired or invalid when its signature is bad or it has expired. With no licence configured, nothing is gated.
data.logs#Logs:
Logs are OpenTelemetry-shaped JSON on stdout, with service.name pulse-backend and the version from APP_VERSION. Lines worth watching:
Log line Meaning refusing to start: ... A fatal startup condition. The rest of the line names it. AUTHENTICATION DISABLED — every request will be rejected as Unauthenticated The session key is one that authz refuses. Fix PULSE_JWT_SECRET. PUBLISHCFG ... What each outward channel is allowed to do grounding: no data/corpus directory The product fact files are missing from the image; whitepapers are written without product facts gRPC reflection ENABLED Reflection is on. It should not be on a deployed instance. security config validated, or a warning listing problems The result of the production gate
data.rate-limiting#Rate limiting: PULSE_RATE_RPS and PULSE_RATE_BURST cap calls per peer IP. Over-limit calls get ResourceExhausted before any other work. Off by default.
data.self-healing#Self-healing:
An in-process watchdog probes local resources and the inference and voice endpoints, and a remediator reacts to what it finds. SelfHealService/GetStatus shows it working: whether the loop is healthy, the last event, recent events, and how many remediations were tried and failed. healthy is false only when the most recent event is critical and was not remediated. The service only observes. It never triggers remediation itself.
Remediation is automatic by default, from a fixed list of non-destructive actions: restart one of PULSE’s model runners, add bounded capacity to one, open the in-process circuit breaker, roll back the loop’s own most recent change to a runner when that change was made shortly before the fault, or notify. A plan outside that list or below the confidence floor becomes a notification. Nothing deletes data, rolls back a release, or touches a security control. See the self-healing operations agent card.
To turn automatic remediation off, set SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS=false. Plans are still reasoned and recorded, but none is applied.
data.the-production-gate#The production gate:
At startup PULSE checks for insecure configuration:
The session key is missing or refused. CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset or contains a wildcard, while the app is not served same-origin through PULSE_WEB_DIR. With PULSE_ENV=production, either problem stops the server with refusing to start in production. Otherwise it is a warning.
A missing or refused session key is the exception: it stops startup on every deployment, whatever PULSE_ENV says, because a server that cannot verify its own sessions has nothing safe to do. What production adds is that the CORS problem stops it too.
TIDE’s k0s overlay sets PULSE_ENV=production on the PulseControlPlane, so a deployment applied from it refuses to start on an insecure configuration. Before applying it to a running instance, confirm the current pod logs security config validated; otherwise the new pod will not start. PULSE_ENV has no other effect: it does not touch billing or plans, and reflection has its own opt-in, PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION.
data.tls#TLS:
Pick one:
Setup How TLS at the edge (usual) Nothing to set. The edge terminates TLS and speaks plain HTTP to PULSE. Direct exposure PULSE_TLS_CERT and PULSE_TLS_KEY. TLS 1.2 minimum, forward-secret AEAD suites only. Service-plane mutual TLS MESH_MTLS=true, with the mesh CA. Every client needs a mesh certificate. TLS 1.3 only. If the CA is unavailable, the server refuses to start rather than downgrade.

data:
PULSE is sold on its own, with its own plans. A PULSE subscription does not include FACE, and a FACE subscription does not include PULSE.
Seats are the whole price. PULSE charges per seat per month. There is no compute meter, no overage, and no per-action or outcome fee on any plan.
data.currency-and-billing-periods#Currency an: There is one US-dollar price list. You are invoiced in your regional currency, converted with the European Central Bank euro reference rates. The rate for a month is the last ECB publication before the 1st. It stays fixed for the whole month. Seat prices round to a whole unit of your currency. Billing periods run from your subscription’s start date (anniversary periods), not from the calendar month. For how the plan reaches the Billing page of a deployment, see Billing.
data.plans#Plans:
Plan Where PULSE runs Seats Price per seat per month Daily tasks Lite Runink’s shared machines 1 to 9 $49 billed yearly, or $59 month-to-month 10 full-speed tasks per seat per day, then a slower pace until midnight Dedicated A dedicated node, or runners in your own cloud account 10 or more $99, billed yearly No daily limit Enterprise Your premises or your own cloud 10 or more Custom quote No daily limit Prices are the US-dollar list. See Currency and billing periods for how your invoice is priced.
Lite runs in the spare capacity of Runink’s shared machines, the way spot capacity works on a public cloud. That is why it is the lowest price.
Dedicated runs PULSE’s work on a node of your own, under a signed annual contract, with no noisy neighbours. Where the compute sits, and whose bill it lands on, is settled in that contract.
Enterprise is quoted to fit the deployment, on your premises or in your own cloud.
No plan sends your data to an outside AI service. See Sovereign inference.
data.the-lite-daily-task-limit#The Lite daily:
Each Lite seat runs its first 10 tasks a day at full speed. After that, every task still runs, on reduced-priority compute, until midnight on that seat’s clock. Nothing is refused for going over, and nothing is billed for it. This limit is part of the Lite plan’s terms.
What counts as a task. One action you start that needs model work: a Site Audit, a radar search, a generated post, a Studio piece, a strategy, an assistant answer, and so on. A task counts once, however many model calls it makes, and only when its first model call starts. An action that ends without model work, such as a validation error, counts nothing. What does not count. Work no seat started: the daily engines, churn watch, publishing, phone calls, and WhatsApp and SMS replies. Whose day. The seat’s own time zone from its settings, or UTC when none is set. What you see. Past the limit, a strip above every page says so and gives the time the count resets, for example “Daily limit reached: tasks keep running on reduced compute until 00:00”. The Billing page shows “Today: X of 10 fast tasks”. If the count cannot be read within a few seconds, the task runs at the slower pace rather than being refused. Dedicated and Enterprise seats have no daily limit: nothing is counted, shown, or slowed for them.
A seat that no subscription covers is refused when it starts a task.

data:
PULSE drafts a great deal on its own: daily social copy, blog posts, podcast episodes, videos. Whether any of it leaves the building is decided by two layers of switches, and nothing is armed by default.
Every switch, with its default and the order to turn them on, is in one table on Switches and arming order.
data.channel-specific-safeguards#Channel-spec: Channel Also needs blog A GitHub data source with a token, PULSE_SITE_REPO, and the content owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS. youtube YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS. Unset means private, so an unreviewed upload is never public by accident. linkedin The token on the user’s LinkedIn card (sealed in the database), else, for a user with no LinkedIn connection, LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN (a person or an organization URN). A company page also needs the app’s Community Management API approval. The content owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS. podcast, audiobook The owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS, PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, and the episode’s audio must exist. Then submit /podcast/feed.xml once to each podcast platform.
data.checking-what-is-armed#Checking what is:
At startup the server logs one line per channel:
PUBLISHCFG youtube: armed=false (...); channel opinion from ...; console config: ... A refused publish logs PUBLISHCFG : DISARMED — did NOT ..., with the layer that decided.
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=yes, on, 1, or TRUE does not arm anything. The server warns at startup with PUBLISHCFG-AMBIGUOUS. Write exactly true.
data.outbound-calls#Outbound calls: CallLead dials through the deployment’s Asterisk trunk and caller ID. It needs PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS=true, which is off by default and independent of PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED, and a caller whose current role is editor or admin.
data.posting-to-linkedin-as-a-company-page#Po:
The LinkedIn card under Settings → Integrations holds the token PULSE posts with. A user who has a LinkedIn connection always posts with it; a disconnected one posts nothing (the deployment token is not used instead). The deployment’s LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN is used only for a user with no LinkedIn connection at all. The server log says which token each post used, and the channel’s readiness (ListChannelReadiness: credential_source, author_kind, author_urn) shows it before anything is posted.
Choose who posts on the card lists the company pages the token may post as (LinkedIn roles ADMINISTRATOR or CONTENT_ADMINISTRATOR). Pick one, and approved posts are authored by urn:li:organization:. Leave it on Me to post as the member; PULSE then reads the member id from LinkedIn (/v2/userinfo, which needs the openid and profile scopes).
Owner action first. LinkedIn lets an app list and post as company pages only after it approves the app for the Community Management API. The token then needs w_organization_social (to post) and rw_organization_admin (to list the pages). Until then the list is empty and the card says why. Every other gate still applies: PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED, PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN, and the owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS.
With the instance’s LinkedIn app configured (LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET) and LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES=true, Connect company pages on the card signs in with the page scopes instead of a pasted token. See LinkedIn.
data.setting-a-channel#Setting a channel:
A channel’s own setting comes from the first of these that holds a clear yes or no:
An environment variable, PULSE_PUBLISH_, for example PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE=false. It accepts 1, t, true, y, yes, on and 0, f, false, n, no, off. A config file, at PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH (default /etc/runink/pulse-publishing.json), or the same JSON inline in PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON when there is no file. The built-in default, which is on. Combined with a kill switch that is off by default, nothing publishes until someone arms the global. The config file accepts either shape:
[{"channel": "youtube", "armed": false}] {"channels": [{"channel": "youtube", "armed": false}]} A channel missing from the file has no opinion. A file that cannot be read or parsed is ignored and changes nothing in either direction.
data.the-channels#The channels: Channel key What it publishes blog A Hugo post on your website, through GitHub. See Site pipeline. podcast Podcast episodes, by adding them to the public RSS feed audiobook The weekly long-form book, in the same feed youtube Real uploads to a YouTube channel, under the operator’s Google identity linkedin Text posts as the connected member, or as the company page chosen on the LinkedIn card. The daily LinkedIn draft is written whatever this says; see below. instagram Has its own control, so the channel is governed by the same switch spotify Has its own control, under the same rule
data.the-daily-linkedin-draft#The daily Linke:
Once a day the social engine writes one LinkedIn post per active campaign: a hook line, short paragraphs, three to five hashtags, and a closing link to PULSE_LINKEDIN_CTA_URL (default https://runink.org). The row belongs to the campaign’s owner and waits on Approval with a Copy draft button, so a person pastes it into LinkedIn.
The draft is never scheduled. The engine writes no scheduled_posts row for it, and it needs no switch to be written. A draft over LinkedIn’s 3,000-character limit is still kept, and its title says OVER 3000 CHARS, trim before posting. A generation that fails, comes back empty, or is only a refusal is logged and not stored. One draft per campaign per day. A restart does not write a second one. Approving a LinkedIn draft still offers it to the LinkedIn publisher. It is recorded withheld, and nothing reaches LinkedIn, when the channel is disarmed (PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN=false or the kill switch off), when no LinkedIn token is configured (neither a connection nor, for a user without one, LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN), or when the owner is not in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS. The content stays approved, ready to copy.
Drafts-only is a setting, not a property of the code. With the kill switch armed, LinkedIn not narrowed, a token configured, and the owner allowlisted, approving a draft posts it. To keep LinkedIn drafts-only while other channels are armed, set PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN=false. A campaign that an audit created is a draft until someone activates it, so an audit on its own produces no daily LinkedIn draft.
data.the-rule#The rule: armed(channel) = PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is exactly "true" AND the channel's own setting is on PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is the kill switch. It is off unless it is exactly the lowercase string true. When it is off, no channel can publish, whatever else is set. Each channel can then be narrowed. A channel with no setting of its own follows the kill switch. A channel setting can only turn a channel off. It can never turn one on when the kill switch is off.
data.the-same-switch-gates-server-writes#The:
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true is also what arms the daily blog drafting in the social engine, and what starts the daily site-audit engine. With it off, neither runs and neither costs model time.
It is not enough for the Site Audit’s apply modes (apply, commit, pr), which write to the server’s filesystem and run git with the server’s credentials. Those also need:
Variable Default Meaning PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY off A narrowing key AND-ed with the kill switch. Unlike the channel keys it defaults off, so arming every channel does not arm server writes. Same yes/no tokens as PULSE_PUBLISH_. PULSE_APPLY_ROOT none The only directory a repo_path may resolve into. Unset refuses every mode, plan included. and the caller must be an administrator, read from the users table on every call.
data.what-disarming-does-to-queued-posts#What:
The kill switch applies at the moment of publishing, not only when a post is queued. A scheduled post that comes due on a disarmed channel is marked withheld, with the reason. That is final. Re-arming does not replay the backlog; schedule the content again to re-queue it.
Approving content does not bypass the switch either. An approval is consent to the content, and the switch is a statement about the channel.
data.who-may-publish-as-the-deployment#Who ma:
Some channels publish with the user’s own connected account (youtube, instagram, spotify), so a user can only ever post as themselves. Others publish as the deployment:
Channel Why it is the deployment’s linkedin The user’s own LinkedIn connection (Settings → Integrations); the deployment’s LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN only for a user with no connection blog The operator’s PULSE_SITE_REPO podcast, audiobook The one public RSS feed at /podcast/feed.xml On these channels, being armed is not enough. The content’s owner must also be listed in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS, a comma-separated list of PULSE user ids (the users.id column, not emails). Empty means nobody.
A dispatch by anyone else is recorded as withheld, with a reason naming the owner gate. It is never reported as posted, and nothing is sent. The daily blog, podcast and audiobook engines skip other users’ campaigns before generating, and log SKIPPED with the same reason. The feed lists only allowlisted owners’ episodes, and only for the channels that are armed. With both podcast and audiobook disarmed, /podcast/feed.xml returns 404. A is the id column of the users table.

data: PULSE can run a company website’s content loop end to end: it writes blog posts and publishes them to the site’s Hugo repository, audits the live site every day, and opens pull requests that fix what the audit finds. Runink runs its own site this way. Each deployment points PULSE at its own site. There are no defaults that name Runink.
data.audit-fix-pull-requests#Audit-fix pull r:
From a relevance audit report, a person can apply the fix artifacts to a site repository (ApplyAuditActions). See Apply the fixes.
Every mode, plan included, needs PULSE_APPLY_ROOT set and a repo_path that resolves inside it. Anything else gets one generic refusal. plan is a dry run. Like every ApplyAuditActions call, it needs an editor or admin (the RBAC write tier). apply, commit, and pr need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true, PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true, and a signed-in administrator. The role is read from the users table on every call, not from the token. In pr mode with a GitHub connection, PULSE opens the pull request against the connection’s owner and repo, on branch seo/pulse-remediation by default, against main. Copy and infrastructure changes are returned as manual and never applied.
data.fixes-proposed-to-the-customers-own-repo: Without any server checkout, a connected website repository (Settings › Integrations, connected by an administrator with a fine-grained token for that one repository) lets an administrator press Propose as pull request on an audit finding. PULSE reads the repository through the GitHub API, places the fix, has the plan gate judge it, and opens one pull request from a new pulse/- branch. It never pushes to the base branch and never merges. It needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true, but not PULSE_APPLY_ROOT. See Website repository.
data.how-a-post-gets-there#How a post gets th: A post is written. Either the social engine drafts one blog article per active campaign per day, or you approve blog-channel content yourself. It is scheduled. The social engine schedules its draft two hours ahead. That window is a chance to cancel it on the Schedule screen before the worker dispatches it. It is published over git. PULSE renders the content as a Hugo post at /.md and, by default, opens a pull request on branch pulse/publish-. Nothing goes live until someone merges it. No third-party social API is involved. The post goes to your own repository with your own GitHub token.
data.settings#Settings: Variable Default Meaning PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED off Must be exactly true. PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY off Audit-fix apply/commit/pr only (not the blog). Must also be on for those modes. PULSE_APPLY_ROOT none The only directory an audit-fix repo_path may point into. Unset refuses every mode. PULSE_PUBLISH_BLOG follows the global Set false to silence only the blog. PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS empty (nobody) User ids whose content may publish to the site. Others are withheld, and their campaigns get no daily draft. PULSE_SITE_REPO none, required owner/repo of your site. PULSE_SITE_BRANCH main Base branch. PULSE_SITE_BLOG_DIR content/blog Where posts go. PULSE_SITE_PUBLISH_MODE pr pr opens a pull request. commit pushes to the base branch and is live at once. PULSE_SITE_AUTHOR omitted The author in the post’s front matter. PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL omitted Your site’s base URL, used for the canonical link. The GitHub token comes from the GitHub connection of the user who owns the content. See Connections.
data.the-daily-site-audit#The daily site audi:
Once a day, at 03:47 UTC, the site audit engine runs the relevance audit against one URL and stores the full report. It also files a readable digest as content on the site_audit channel. That channel is not publishable: the digest exists to be read.
Variable Meaning PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED Must be exactly true, or the engine does not start at all. One autonomy switch covers the engine and the publishers alike. PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL The site to audit. PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL Used when PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL is unset. Disarmed, the engine logs Site Audit Engine: NOT started — autonomy is disarmed (PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is not "true"). Armed but with no target, it logs Site Audit Engine: NOT started — no target site; set PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL (or PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL).
The first audit after a deploy waits for the next 03:47 UTC slot. Run one on demand from Site Audit at any time. Each audit is limited to 10 minutes. A run that scored nothing, for example because the site was unreachable, is recorded as a failure rather than a result.
The engine audits and records. It never fixes. Fixing stays a human decision.
data.when-it-refuses#When it refuses: Message Cause website publishing is disabled: ... The blog channel is not armed. The message names the layer that decided. no github integration/token configured for user ... The content’s owner has no GitHub connection. PULSE_SITE_REPO is not set — refusing to publish; set it to YOUR site repo as owner/repo No target repository. invalid site repo "...": expected owner/repo The repository is malformed. refusing to publish empty content The post has no title or body. The daily blog drafting only runs while the blog channel is armed. A disarmed channel costs no model time.

data:
Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine ships with every outward action switched off. This page lists each switch in one place: what it defaults to, what it does, and the order to turn them on safely. The detail behind each one is on Publishing controls and Users and access.
Set these on TIDE’s PulseControlPlane resource or its overlay, never on the live Deployment. The operator puts back anything changed on the Deployment.
data.arm-automations-only-if-you-need-them#Ar: Set PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS=true once the channels the automations use are armed and allowlisted. Each automation still runs by itself only after its owner arms it, and every step runs with the owner’s role.
data.arm-outbound-calls-only-if-you-need-them:
Set PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS=true once the Asterisk settings are in place and the compliance work for calling real numbers is done. See Telephony and messaging.
To disarm, reverse the order, or simply unset PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED: that stops every channel, the audit-apply modes and the daily site-audit engine at once. It also stops every automation’s outbound steps. It does not stop outbound calls, WhatsApp and SMS replies, or self-healing, each of which has its own key.
data.arm-server-writes-only-if-you-need-them#: To let administrators apply Site Audit fixes, set PULSE_APPLY_ROOT to the directory that holds the site checkouts, then PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true. Leave both unset to keep the server read-only. The same two switches arm Propose as pull request on a connected website repository (Settings › Integrations › Website repository), which needs no PULSE_APPLY_ROOT: it writes only to a new pulse/ branch on GitHub and opens a pull request for a person to merge.
data.arm-the-kill-switch#Arm the kill switch: Set PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true. Check one PUBLISHCFG : armed=… line per channel, and that the audit-apply line still says armed=false.
data.checked-against-the-code#Checked against: Every key on this page is read by the backend (grpc/cmd, grpc/internal) or, for AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS and PULSE_JWT_SECRET, by the shared security library it uses. The backend also reads these keys, which arm nothing and are listed on the configuration reference: PULSE_SKILLS_MODELS, PULSE_SEARCH_MIN_GAP_MS, LINKEDIN_API_BASE, LINKEDIN_API_VERSION, LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN, LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN, GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENDPOINT, MESH_ISSUER_URL, MESH_ISSUER_TOKEN_FILE, FFMPEG_PATH and the rest of the storage, inference, telephony and billing settings.
data.confirm-the-production-gate-passes#Confi: With PULSE_ENV=production, the server refuses to start on an insecure configuration. Before setting it, confirm that the current pod logs security config validated. See Operations.
data.image-build-arguments#Image build argume:
The backend image (grpc/Dockerfile) takes its base images through two build arguments, each base pinned by digest. Point them at a registry mirror and the same digests come from there.
Build argument Default Bases BASE_REGISTRY docker.io/library golang:1.26-bookworm (build) and debian:bookworm-slim (runtime) FLUTTER_SDK_REGISTRY localhost:5000/runink flutter-sdk:3.47.7 (web bundle) BASE_REGISTRY defaults to the upstream registry. The Flutter SDK image is built by the platform and served from the cluster’s own registry, so a build elsewhere needs FLUTTER_SDK_REGISTRY pointed at a registry that holds it.
data.let-accounts-run-on-autopilot-only-if-yo: Autopilot is switched on per account by its owner, under Settings › Integrations › Autopilot. It adds no server key: it sends only through channels you armed above, so a channel you narrowed stays off for Autopilot too. To stop every Autopilot post at once, unset PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED (or the channel’s PULSE_PUBLISH_): queued posts are then recorded withheld when they come due and are never replayed when you re-arm.
data.messaging-a-lead-at-their-own-number#Mes:
Do it on a lead’s WhatsApp or SMS step can text the lead’s own number, not only a contact an admin added. Every rule below is enforced on the server:
SMS only, after a confirm tap. The person sees the exact text and the masked number, and taps to send. It still needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS not switched off. Only a number with a recorded source. A phone number counts only when PULSE recorded where it came from: the lead’s own web page (the audit), a person typing it into PULSE, your website form, or HubSpot. The Leads page shows the source. A number without a source is never texted. STOP is honoured. A reply of STOP (also STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT, PARAR, SAIR, BAJA, ARRET) is recorded for that number. After that, the lead’s step no longer offers WhatsApp or SMS, and a message that was already previewed is refused when confirmed. START, YES or UNSTOP lifts the block. When Twilio itself refuses a send because the number unsubscribed (error 21610), PULSE records the same block. For the replies to reach PULSE, set the Twilio number’s “A message comes in” webhook to /comms/twilio/inbound. PULSE checks Twilio’s signature on every request, and the webhook refuses everything (503) while no auth token is set. WhatsApp needs an approved template. Meta only lets a business start a WhatsApp conversation with a template it has approved. The shared carrier sends plain text only, so PULSE never starts a WhatsApp conversation with a lead. Do it says so plainly and offers SMS or email instead. WhatsApp to a contact an admin added works as before.
data.name-who-may-publish-as-the-deployment#N: Set PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS to the owner’s , read from the id column of the users table. Do this before arming, so that the moment the kill switch goes on, only the owner’s content can leave on LinkedIn, the blog, or the podcast feed.
data.narrow-the-channels-you-do-not-want#Narr: Set PULSE_PUBLISH_=false for each channel that must stay off, including PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN=false if LinkedIn is to stay drafts-only, PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL=false if users must not send email from PULSE, and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP=false / PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS=false if nobody may message from PULSE. Narrowing first means arming the global turns on only what you meant.
data.pulse_envproduction#\u003ccode\u003ePULS:
TIDE’s k0s overlay sets PULSE_ENV=production on the PulseControlPlane, so it takes effect when that resource is applied. With it set, the server refuses to start, logging refusing to start in production, when:
the session key (PULSE_JWT_SECRET) is missing or is one the platform refuses, or the app is not served same-origin (PULSE_WEB_DIR is empty) and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset or contains *. A missing or refused session key stops startup whatever PULSE_ENV says; what production adds is that the CORS problem stops it too, instead of warning.
PULSE_ENV also changes one TLS log line. It does nothing else: no billing, metering, or plan behavior reads it, and it does not turn reflection on or off.
data.safe-arming-order#Safe arming order: Turn things on one at a time, and check the startup log after each restart.
data.set-up-the-sign-in-apps-if-people-should: Set an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL routed by the TIDE edge, then the app clients: META_APP_ID / META_APP_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID / LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET. None of them publishes anything: connecting only stores a sealed token. What each developer console needs is on Setup. Leave LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES off until LinkedIn has approved the Community Management API for the app.
data.the-switches#The switches: Key Default Effect PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED off The global kill switch for every outward channel, the first half of the audit-apply gate, and what starts the daily site-audit engine. While it is off, nothing publishes, and approving a draft does not queue it at its planned date. PULSE_PUBLISH_ follows the kill switch Narrows one channel: BLOG, PODCAST, AUDIOBOOK, YOUTUBE, INSTAGRAM, SPOTIFY, LINKEDIN, EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS. Can only turn a channel off. PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM follows the kill switch Approving (or a schedule or Autopilot reaching) an Instagram piece publishes it by what it is: a post (one photo, with caption, hashtags and alt text), a carousel (its rendered 1080×1350 slides), a Reel (the owner’s own video, attached in Studio; MP4/MOV, 3 s to 15 min, at most 300 MB and 1920 px wide, index at the start) or Stories (each attached photo or video, 3 to 60 s; no caption, and stickers cannot be posted through the API). A Reel or Story with no video of the owner’s gets one made by PULSE at approval (or on download), and so does a YouTube Short (9:16, at most 3 min, uploaded through PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE like any video; the owner’s own video goes first): the script’s lines drawn as frames in the account’s brand colours with burned-in captions; Instagram’s API publishes no stickers, so a Story’s stickers are drawn as still cards and listed on a checklist in caption.txt to add by hand, read aloud by ttsd (TTSD_URL; none = a silent video that says “no voiceover: speech service unavailable”), assembled by ffmpeg (H.264 + AAC, 30 fps, one at a time, 2 threads, 2 min per encode; Reels at most 90 s, Stories split into parts of at most 60 s); a server without ffmpeg says “video is not available on this server”. A piece without its media is refused for scheduling and withheld at approval with “needs a video / photo: upload one in Studio”. Instagram fetches every file from PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL at an unguessable, signed address that expires within two hours; without that URL the channel is not ready. Before publishing PULSE reads the account’s content_publishing_limit; at the limit the post moves to after the 24-hour window with the reason. Needs the Instagram professional account connected with instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish (Meta app review); a missing permission is recorded as “reconnect Instagram to allow …”. META_APP_ID, META_APP_SECRET unset The instance’s own Meta app (Facebook Login for Business). With both set, Settings › Integrations shows Connect with Instagram: the person signs in at Facebook, PULSE stores a sealed long-lived token, finds the Instagram professional account through their Page, and renews the token in its last ten days (a failed renewal is shown on the card). The app must allow the redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/social/callback. Unset: the card says sign-in is not set up and accepts a pasted token instead. LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET unset The instance’s own LinkedIn app. With both set (and an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL), the LinkedIn card shows Connect with LinkedIn: the person signs in at LinkedIn (openid profile w_member_social), PULSE stores the sealed token and the member, and approved LinkedIn posts use that token. LinkedIn tokens last 60 days; PULSE renews them only when LinkedIn issued a refresh token, otherwise the card shows “reconnect before” the date. The app must allow the redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/social/callback. Unset: the card accepts a pasted token instead. PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN and PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS still decide whether anything is posted. LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES off Set true only once LinkedIn approved the app for the Community Management API. The card then offers Connect company pages, which also asks for r_organization_social, w_organization_social and rw_organization_admin, and lists the pages the member administers to post as. PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL follows the kill switch Send on a lead’s email draft (SendOutreachEmail): one email, sent when the user taps Send, from that user’s own connected mailbox (Gmail, Microsoft 365 or SMTP, see Connections). There is no shared sender, so PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS does not apply. Off, a send is recorded withheld and the sheet keeps Copy and Open in email. Editors and admins only. PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP, PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS follows the kill switch A WhatsApp message or SMS through the shared Twilio carrier: Do it on a lead’s next step under Leads › To do today, and Send on a result. Each send needs the person to confirm its preview. Recipients are the contacts an admin added under Settings › Messaging, plus, for SMS only, the person’s own open leads whose phone number has a recorded source (see below). Off, the send is refused as “not configured” with the switch named; nothing is sent. Calls are not affected. PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN_REPLIES, PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_REPLIES, PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE_REPLIES follows the kill switch Replies PULSE sends from the Autopilot reply queue (Campaigns › Approvals): an answer to a comment (and, on Instagram, to a post that tags the account). A reply needs this switch and the channel’s own PULSE_PUBLISH_, so false here keeps posting on and answering off. Off, an approved reply is recorded withheld with the switch named; nothing is sent. PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS follows the kill switch Answers to Instagram direct messages from the reply queue. Needs PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM too. Independently of every switch, a message is answered only within 24 hours of the person’s last message (Meta’s window); after that the reply is withheld with that reason. PULSE_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT 50 Emails one user may send in any 24 hours, to protect their mailbox’s reputation. A positive whole number; anything else means 50. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET unset The instance’s own Google OAuth client. Also used for sign-in and token refresh. Needed for Connect Gmail, which asks for gmail.send and, to see replies, gmail.readonly. Also Connect with YouTube (asks for youtube.upload, youtube.force-ssl, yt-analytics.readonly; redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/social/callback must be allowed on the client). Unset: the YouTube card accepts a pasted token instead. The same client connects Google Search Console (read-only webmasters.readonly, redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/search-console/callback); see Google. MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID unset, unset, common The instance’s own Microsoft Entra app registration, for Connect Microsoft 365 (delegated Mail.Send, Mail.Read for replies, User.Read, offline_access). Set the secret from the instance’s configuration, never from a repository secret. PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH, PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON /etc/runink/pulse-publishing.json, none The same per-channel opinions as a file, or inline JSON. An environment key wins over the file. PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS empty, which means nobody User ids (the users.id column, not emails) allowed to publish through the channels that post as the deployment: LinkedIn, blog, podcast, and audiobook. Anyone else’s dispatch is recorded withheld. Settings › Integrations › Active (per user, not an env var) every channel active until the user saves A channel its owner switched off gets no daily drafts, and its queued posts are recorded withheld: channel not active. It can only narrow: it never arms a channel the switches above leave off. PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN follows the kill switch Keep this false to keep LinkedIn drafts-only. See the daily LinkedIn draft. Settings › Integrations › Autopilot (per account, not an env var) off for every account After a person approves a post, PULSE queues it at the account’s best time instead of sending it at once, and the publishing worker sends it through the same gate as any scheduled post: the kill switch, PULSE_PUBLISH_, PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS and the Active switch above all still decide at send time. Autopilot never queues content nobody approved, and never queues on a disarmed channel (the approval then sends, and is recorded withheld, as before). It pauses the account by itself on an expired connection, a rate limit, or three failed sends in a row, and says so under Leads › To do today with a Reconnect link; transient failures are retried with backoff (5, 20, 80 minutes). Turning Autopilot off withholds its queued posts. See Autopilot and agencies. Autopilot › Answer simple comments by itself (per account) off Replies to comments PULSE reads (LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube; on Instagram also mentions and direct messages) are drafted into Campaigns › Approvals. A person may let three low-risk kinds go out by themselves: thanks, an answer taken from approved FAQ content, and a link to the business’s own site. Each one must pass OpenBias and the plan gate (a concur verdict; with PULSE_JUDGEMENT=off nothing replies by itself) and is logged on its row. A reply is an outbound post on the channel, so it also needs the kill switch, PULSE_PUBLISH_, the channel’s reply switch (PULSE_PUBLISH__REPLIES, or PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS for a direct message), the publisher allowlist and the Active switch. PULSE_LINKEDIN_CTA_URL https://runink.org The address the daily LinkedIn draft ends with. PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY off The second half of the audit-apply gate. With the kill switch, it allows the Site Audit’s apply, commit, and pr modes, and Propose as pull request on the website repository, for administrators only. Off (or the kill switch off) refuses both before anything is read from or sent to GitHub. Settings › Integrations › Website repository (per account, not an env var) not connected The customer’s own site repository on GitHub, with a fine-grained token limited to that repository (Contents and Pull requests: read and write), sealed with the envelope key. An administrator connects it; the card shows connected, missing permission, token rejected, branch not found or unreachable. A proposal is one branch pulse/- and one pull request through the GitHub API: PULSE never pushes to the base branch, never merges, never edits .github/workflows/ or .git/, refuses .. paths and links, and caps a proposal at 20 files, 256 KiB each and 1 MiB in all. The plan gate judges the edit before the pull request is opened; a dissent opens nothing. PULSE_APPLY_ROOT unset, which refuses every mode The only directory a Site Audit repo_path may resolve into. Applies to plan too. PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS off Lets automations (the automation card a person opens on a lead or a campaign item) do outbound work: schedule a post, write to HubSpot, send email from the owner’s mailbox, and place AI calls (which also need PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS, PULSE_AI_CALLS and the lead’s consent record). Under the kill switch: both must be on, and each step still needs its own channel switch and the publisher allowlist. Each automation must also be armed by its owner; a dry run never sends. PULSE_OPPORTUNITIES_DISCOVERY on The daily read of open procurement data (EU TED, UK Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, Brazil PNCP, CanadaBuys, and US SAM.gov for accounts that added their own key) and of requests for proposals found by PULSE’s crawler, for every account with an offering to match. Reading only: nothing is sent or submitted, and the kill switch does not apply. Off stops the daily read; “Look now” on Opportunities still reads for the person who presses it. Drafting a response (on request, or the opt-in auto-draft) spends model time on the account’s own inference. PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS off Allows CallLead to dial through the deployment’s Asterisk trunk. Independent of the kill switch. The caller must also be an editor or admin. PULSE_AI_CALLS off Allows AI voice calls to leads (AICallService.PlaceAICall, AI calls). Needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS as well, an editor or admin, Twilio voice settings, PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (https), and for each lead a recorded consent, a time zone and a drafted call script. PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL unset The public origin for absolute podcast-feed links, and the base of the mailbox OAuth callback /oauth/mail/callback. Without it, an armed feed answers 503 instead of rendering links nobody can fetch, and Gmail / Microsoft 365 cannot be connected (SMTP still can). It must be https for Connect with Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and Search Console to be offered, and for Instagram to fetch media; the TIDE edge must route /oauth/social/callback and /oauth/search-console/callback to PULSE. See Public address and redirects. PULSE_JUDGEMENT on off turns the plan gate off: proposals are no longer judged before they are saved, and Autopilot answers nothing by itself (an auto-reply needs a concur verdict). Leave it on. TTSD_URL the in-cluster ttsd Service TIDE’s shared text-to-speech service, as a full URL. Set to empty to turn voice output off: Reels and Stories PULSE makes are then silent and say so, and read-back and podcast audio are unavailable. Sends nothing outward by itself. PULSE_ENV unset production (any case) turns the startup security check from a warning into a refusal to start. TIDE’s k0s overlay sets it. See below. PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION off true turns on gRPC reflection. For local work only; PULSE_ENV does not affect it. AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS empty, which means nobody Who may sign in with Google. AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY off Exactly true hides the password form. AUTH_SEED_USERS unset Operator-granted roles as email=persona,…, re-applied at every start. See Seeded roles. SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS on An explicit no stops the self-healing loop applying anything; plans are still reasoned and recorded. See Operations. PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY off An explicit yes lets PULSE answer inbound WhatsApp and SMS messages with a model-written reply. Each reply is a send, so it also needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP (or PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS for an SMS) not switched off. Off, messages are still received and nothing is answered. See Telephony and messaging. Every switch is also reported at startup. Look for the PUBLISHCFG lines, including PUBLISHCFG audit-apply: armed=…; PULSE_APPLY_ROOT set=…; callers must be admin, and for security config validated.
data.yes-and-no-values#Yes and no values:
The keys do not all parse yes and no the same way, and the difference matters:
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED arms only on the exact value true. yes, on, 1, and TRUE leave it off, and the server warns with PUBLISHCFG-AMBIGUOUS. PULSE_PUBLISH_, PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS, PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY, PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS and PULSE_AI_CALLS accept 1, t, true, y, yes, on and 0, f, false, n, no, off, in any case. Anything else, including empty, counts as unset, which for the last four means off. AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY is on only for the exact value true. PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION is on for true in any case. SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS and PULSE_OPPORTUNITIES_DISCOVERY default to on, so they read the other way round: they take the same tokens, and unset or unparseable leaves them on. Only an explicit no turns them off. PULSE_JUDGEMENT is on unless set to off (any case). LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES is on for 1, t, T, true, TRUE or True; anything else, including yes, leaves it off. PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY takes the same tokens and is off unless set to an explicit yes.

data:
PULSE has four voice and messaging paths. All of them are off until you configure them.
The carrier settings themselves are admin-only, and they live on the Account page under Messaging & calls — not in the navigation rail. Someone who is not an admin of this instance never sees the carrier fields.
data.browser-voice-calls#Browser voice calls:
The app’s full-screen call view sends a WebRTC offer to /voice/webrtc/offer. PULSE forwards it to the platform’s shared calling agent at CALLING_AGENT_URL, which carries the audio. PULSE is only the authenticated signaling door.
When CALLING_AGENT_URL is unset, the offer is refused with HTTP 503 and voice calling is not configured: CALLING_AGENT_URL is unset. For signaling tests, PULSE_WEBRTC_SIGNALING_ONLY=true answers offers with PULSE’s local handler, which carries no audio.
Turn-based voice input (/voice/transcribe) needs only the Voxtral server (VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL). Both voice endpoints require a signed-in caller.
data.outbound-calls-to-leads-asterisk#Outboun:
Leads → Call (LeadService.CallLead) places a real phone call through a self-hosted Asterisk PBX. There is no per-minute calling SaaS.
PULSE asks Asterisk’s REST interface (ARI) to dial the lead into a dialplan context. That context runs AudioSocket() back to PULSE’s audio listener, passing the call’s ID: AudioSocket(${PULSE_CALL_ID},:), where is the port in AUDIOSOCKET_ADDR. PULSE sets PULSE_CALL_ID on every call it places. The ID is how a call finds its own cold-call script; without it the call runs with no script. PULSE transcribes the caller (Voxtral), answers with the sales agent, speaks the reply (Runink TIDE’s shared ttsd, TTSD_URL), and streams it back. Variable Meaning AUDIOSOCKET_ADDR The TCP listener Asterisk connects to ASTERISK_ARI_URL, ASTERISK_ARI_USER, ASTERISK_ARI_PASSWORD ARI access. Leave empty to keep outbound calls off. PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS Must be true (or another yes) for CallLead to dial. Off by default. Only editors and admins may place calls. ASTERISK_ENDPOINT_PATTERN The dial string, with {number} substituted ASTERISK_CONTEXT, ASTERISK_EXTENSION The dialplan target that runs AudioSocket() ASTERISK_CALLER_ID Outbound caller ID If ARI is configured and the audio listener cannot bind, the server refuses to start. Otherwise it would place calls it cannot carry: the lead would answer to silence. When ARI is not configured, a failed bind is only a warning.
Without ARI, CallLead returns outbound calling isn't configured — set up Asterisk and ..., naming the missing variables.
Outbound cold calling is regulated. Consent, calling hours, do-not-call lists, and recording disclosure are the operator’s responsibility.
data.send--call-to-a-saved-contact#Send / Cal:
PULSE also carries the shared Runink Send / Call layer, the same code FACE and TIDE use, so the allowlist, the per-send confirmation, the rate limit, the body cap, the recording notice and the audit trail behave identically across the three.
Only a saved contact can be reached. Admins add contacts on Account → Messaging & calls; a number that is not on the list is refused. A service account can never message or call anyone. The carrier settings are sealed with TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK. Without that key the page refuses to store a secret rather than writing it in the clear. Contacts, sealed settings and the delivery trail live under $PULSE_DATA_DIR/comms. Variables. TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN come from the secret store (with an environment fallback); TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER and TWILIO_VOICE_FROM are settings. TWILIO_VOICE_FROM is optional and falls back to TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER. What an admin saves on the page overlays the environment. Delivery states are posted back to /comms/twilio/status. Without PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL there is no callback URL to give the carrier, so states stay at accepted. A call speaks and ends. It plays the recording notice first, then PULSE’s greeting and the summary; there is no interactive media leg on this path.
data.whatsapp-and-sms#WhatsApp and SMS:
PULSE accepts inbound WhatsApp and SMS messages from Twilio at /twilio/message, and answers with its marketing personas: the same set it offers over A2A.
Every request must carry a valid Twilio signature (TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN). Only senders who are contacts in PULSE’s HubSpot account may talk to it. PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID picks whose HubSpot connection is used. The default is to deny. The edge generates text: analysis, content, strategy, research. Creating leads or campaigns and approving content stay behind the signed-in gRPC API. Replies are automatic only when switched on (below). Each one passes PULSE’s guardrails, and the incoming message is treated as data, never as instructions. Replies run as the user set in PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID; with none set, nothing is answered. Automatic replies are off by default. To turn them on, set PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY=true; each reply is a send, so it also needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP (or PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS) not switched off. Otherwise messages are received but not answered. Variable Meaning TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN The Twilio account TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER The WhatsApp sender and the SMS number PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID The user whose HubSpot contacts form the allowlist, and as whom replies run PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY true turns automatic replies on (they also need the publish switches). Default: off

data: PULSE keeps its own accounts in the users table. Each account has one role: admin, editor, or viewer. There are three ways an account comes to exist.
data.google-sign-in#Google sign-in:
Set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID to turn on Sign in with Google, and set AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS to the people allowed to use it. Google sign-in fails closed:
Situation Result GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset No Google button. The exchange endpoint answers google sign-in not configured (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset). Allowlist empty Nobody signs in with Google. The user sees google sign-in is not available on this instance. Email not on the allowlist Refused with this account is not authorized for this instance. First sign-in of an allowed email A new viewer account with an unusable random password. Email removed from the allowlist while signed in The next request is refused with PermissionDenied (this account is no longer on this PULSE instance's sign-in allowlist), and /auth/refresh answers 403. The allowlist is re-checked on every authenticated request (gRPC, HTTP routes, A2A, media) and on every refresh, not only at sign-in. Removing an address, or a TIDE add_users grant expiring, ends that person’s access at once instead of when their refresh token runs out. With no allowlist configured (a local, password-only run) there is nothing to re-check. The break-glass admin is exempt.
Set AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY=true to hide the password form. The break-glass admin still exists, but the app no longer shows the form to reach it.
data.seeded-roles#Seeded roles:
AUTH_SEED_USERS grants roles by email, as a comma-separated list of email=persona pairs. Runink TIDE’s operator projects it from the ClientInstance’s user list. It is applied at every start, and it is the roster: it applies exactly, downwards as well as upwards.
Persona Role admin, org_admin, owner admin writer, editor editor reader, viewer viewer A seeded email that has no account yet gets one with an unusable password, so that person signs in with Google. A listed user whose persona is now lower is lowered to it. An admin or editor the seed no longer lists, or lists with an unknown persona, is demoted to viewer (the log says Seeding: demoted …). Whether that person may still sign in at all is decided by AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS. The break-glass admin (PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL) is never raised, lowered or disabled by the seed.
