If every entry is malformed, nobody is demoted and the log says AUTH_SEED_USERS is set but grants nothing PULSE recognises.
data.sessions#Sessions:
Sessions live in the sealed app root, not in the database, so every replica sees the same state.
An access token lasts 24 hours. A refresh token lasts 7 days and works once. A session lasts at most 30 days. Signing out revokes the session and every token issued in it. The Account page can end all of a person’s sessions on every device. It also carries Appearance, the person’s own light or dark preference. Tokens issued before server-side sessions existed carry no session ID and are refused. Those users sign in again once.
data.the-admin-page#The Admin page:
Admin lives inside the Account page. There is no Admin entry in the navigation rail: an admin opens Account, which leads with Admin (the way into Members) and then Messaging & calls. Someone who is not an admin of this instance sees neither section. Members itself is the shared Runink members page (runink.ui.access.v1.AccessService) at /admin: list members, invite, change a role, remove. The server reads the caller’s role fresh from the users table on every call, not from the token, and refuses anyone who is not an admin of this instance.
Billing is not under Account. Plan, seats and usage are their own destination beside it; see Billing.
What a change does depends on where the roster lives:
Deployment What happens to a change PULSE may patch its own ClientInstance (PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE is set and the pod has permission) Written to the ClientInstance first, then to the users table. It is pending until the operator re-projects the roster and PULSE restarts. AUTH_SEED_USERS is set, but PULSE cannot write the ClientInstance Refused, with a sentence saying where access is changed. A local change would be undone at the next start. Neither The users table is the roster. Changes apply at once. When a role changes, PULSE ends that person’s sessions, so the new role takes effect at their next sign-in (the RBAC gate already applies it within seconds). PULSE keeps no seat roster, so invites are not limited by the number of seats on the subscription.
PULSE serves one instance per deployment. Its ID is PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE, else TENANT_ID, else pulse.
data.the-break-glass-admin#The break-glass ad:
When PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD is set, the server creates or updates an account named admin with the admin role at every start. Change the username or email with PULSE_ADMIN_USERNAME and PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL.
Without the variable, the log says No admin password injected (PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD/ADMIN_PASSWORD unset) — skipping admin seed; break-glass login unavailable until one is provided.
This is an emergency account. Give it a strong password from the secret store, and use Google sign-in and seeded roles for everyday access.
data.what-each-role-may-call#What each role m:
Every RPC has a minimum role. The gate runs in both the unary and the streaming interceptor and fails closed: a method with no entry is refused for everyone, admins included, and the build will not pass until it has one. The role comes from the caller’s users row (cached for at most 5 seconds), never from the token’s role claim, so a demotion takes effect within seconds even for a token that is still valid.
Tier Who Covers public anyone, before sign-in IdentityService/Login, ModelService/GetModelStatus session any signed-in account, even one with no recognised role IdentityService/GetCurrentUser, Logout read viewer, editor, admin every List* / Get* of your own records, the activity stream, exports, AuditPipelineService/GetAuditRun and ListAuditRuns, RadarService/ListDiscoveredChannels and ListTrendingPosts write editor, admin everything that generates (spends model time) or changes data: all Generate*, ModelService/Complete, AuditPipelineService/RunAudit and ApplyAuditActions, live Radar research, lead create/scrape/outreach, CallLead and SendOutreachEmail, campaign, content, publishing and integration changes admin admin the Admin page (AccessService) and the messaging contacts and carrier settings A viewer can therefore read every page but cannot run an audit, generate, or approve. New Google accounts start as viewer (see above), so an admin or the seed must raise them before they can work.
Some write-tier calls have a stricter gate in their handler as well: ApplyAuditActions apply/commit/pr need an admin and PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY; CallLead needs PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS. See Publishing controls.
If the server cannot read the caller’s role, the call fails with Unavailable: RBAC: could not read your role, never with an allow.

data:
The API of Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine is gRPC, package pulse.v1. The contracts are the .proto files in grpc/api/proto/pulse/v1/. Browsers use gRPC-Web on the same port. Clients use the generated stubs (Go in grpc/api/v1/, Dart in flutter/lib/core/grpc/). The few plain HTTP routes are listed under HTTP endpoints . To call the API, see Calling the API.
The service pages below are generated from the protos and from the server’s role table (grpc/cmd/rbac_policy.go) by go run ./tools/apidoc, and a test fails when they fall behind, so every method listed is one the server has.
HTTP endpoints Brand analysis and auditsAudit pipeline, diagnosis, research, Search Console, website repository Leads, opportunities and accountsLeads, Opportunities, AI calls, Integrations, agencies Campaigns and resultsCampaigns, plans, Autopilot, automations, metrics Studio and contentContent, Studio, skills, publishing AI and platformModel, activity, identity, config, self-heal Shared componentsBilling, Connections, Profile, Access, Voice, Comms Common typescommons.proto and unused types
data.conventions#Conventions: Authentication. Every method needs authorization: Bearer , except the ones whose least role is “none (public)” and gRPC reflection. The browser client authenticates with a session cookie instead; see Calling the API. Roles. Each method has a least role, read fresh from your account on every call: viewer for reads that spend no model time and change nothing, editor for anything that generates, writes, dials out or places a call, and admin for access and messaging settings. A call below your role fails with PermissionDenied. “Any signed-in” methods (who am I, sign out) work for an account with no role. Some methods check more than the role (an admin row, an arming switch); the page notes say which. Scoping. Data is scoped to the signed-in user. Request fields named user_id do not let you read another user’s data. Streaming. AI generators return stream StreamChunk. See Common types. Errors. Standard gRPC status codes with a human-readable message. See Troubleshooting.

data: Model access, the agent-activity feed, sign-in, the business profile and self-healing status. Package pulse.v1; the least role of each method is in its table.
data.activityservice#ActivityService:
ActivityService is the agent-activity plane: what the CALLER’s agents are doing right now, across every page and tab, not only the one that started them.
AUTHORISATION IS OWNERSHIP. Every run is stamped server-side with the authenticated user of the request that caused it; a subscriber receives a run (replayed or live) only when that owner is its own authenticated identity. Runs with no owner (schedules, webhooks, A2A) are delivered to nobody. The session below is a filter within the caller’s own runs, never authorisation.
WHY THIS EXISTS. PULSE’s generation RPCs stream to their own caller, so a long job is legible only on the screen that launched it. A 15-page whitepaper is minutes of decode on the shared CPU inference plane, and every other page — and every other tab — shows nothing at all. The steps were already being recorded: modelServer.recordInference builds a costed telemetry.RunTrace for every generation (model, tokens, latency, provenance) and hands it to the health reporter. No RPC exposed them, so the cockpit could not show them.
Mirrors FACE’s service of the same name deliberately: same shapes, same replay contract, so the two cockpits can share a mental model and, later, a widget.
pulse.v1.ActivityService, declared in activity.proto.
Method Request → Response Least role Notes SubscribeAgentActivity SubscribeAgentActivityRequest → stream SubscribeAgentActivityResponse viewer SubscribeAgentActivity streams agent runs and their steps as they happen. ON SUBSCRIBE IT REPLAYS THE CURRENT STATE FIRST — every in-flight run, each with the steps recorded so far — before any live event, terminated by snapshot_complete. A client that only saw future events would show nothing to someone who opened the page mid-run, which is the whole failure this plane exists to end. Keying off current state rather than a transition is the rule here. ListFeaturedMessages ListFeaturedMessagesRequest → ListFeaturedMessagesResponse viewer ListFeaturedMessages returns the operator-curated messages the cockpit cycles through — sponsor and partner copy. Served from a file the deployment can mount, so it changes without rebuilding the app. message SubscribeAgentActivityRequest { // Cap on how many trailing steps the initial replay carries per run. 0 uses // the server default. int32 replay_steps_per_run = 1; // Show only those of the caller's OWN runs belonging to this session. // // Empty here falls back to the caller's `x-agent-trace-id` metadata, so a // client that forgets this field is still narrowed to its own tab. With BOTH // absent the subscription is every run the caller owns — never anyone // else's, whatever session is or is not sent. // // WHY THIS EXISTS (FACE's rationale, which applies verbatim here — see // face/grpc/api/proto/semantics/v1/activity.proto). Ambient-for-everyone was // the wrong default for the CUSTOMER cockpit. Every page rendered the same // card for a run nobody on that device had started, so the card and the page // contradicted each other: a centre said "nothing has run on this device yet" // while the card beneath it showed an agent mid-flight. Two true statements // about two different scopes, stacked, reading as a bug. // // THE EMITTER HALF IS LIVE TOO, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS FIELD USABLE. Every // PULSE run started from a request carries the caller's trace id: // model_server.go's startInference (the streaming and the structured // generation paths), the assistant's grounding phase, both editorial-guard // phases (model_server.go and egress.go), and the diagnostic's grounding // phase. That last one used to pass its own diagnosticID, which was the wrong // identifier for the same reason a run id would be — the cockpit subscribes // ONCE for the whole card, so a run stamped with a per-job identity is matched // by no subscriber and disappears from the card of the person who started it. // // A RUN WITH NO SESSION IS NOT SEEN BY A SCOPED CLIENT. Work started off a // context detached from any request — a schedule, a WhatsApp inbound, A2A, // the autonomous media buyer — has no cockpit behind it, so it carries no // session, and no authenticated caller, so it has no owner and reaches no // subscriber at all. The hub gives a scoped subscriber only its OWN runs: // "unattributed" and "somebody else's" are one bucket, not two. That is FACE's // rule as well, and it is what stops a customer's card showing an agent // mid-flight under a page that correctly says nothing has run on this device. // The cost is that an emitter which forgets to thread the session makes its // runs vanish rather than leak — a quiet failure, which is why every emitter // is pinned by test (activity_wire_test.go). string session = 2; } enum AgentRunStatus { AGENT_RUN_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0; AGENT_RUN_STATUS_RUNNING = 1; AGENT_RUN_STATUS_DONE = 2; AGENT_RUN_STATUS_FAILED = 3; } // AgentStep mirrors mesh/telemetry.Step — one unit of agent work. // // PULSE has no multi-step ReAct loop, so a generation is ONE step and `thought` // is normally empty; the useful fields here are model, tokens and latency. A // renderer must not assume every step narrates itself. message AgentStep { string run_id = 1; int32 index = 2; string thought = 3; string action = 4; string input = 5; string result = 6; string model = 7; int64 latency_ms = 8; string error = 9; int64 at_unix = 10; int64 total_tokens = 11; // The step's STABLE, MACHINE-READABLE kind — one of the ~20 tokens in // mesh/telemetry/stepcode.go, e.g. "STEP_DISPATCHED". // // WHY A CODE AND NOT A SENTENCE. A sentence written in Go cannot be // translated by a Flutter client: this app ships four locales and an English // string that arrived over the wire is useless in three of them. A code also // makes the TRUST LEVEL legible — a renderer can badge STEP_MODEL_THOUGHT as // the model's own words and treat STEP_FINISHED as an observed fact, which is // impossible when both arrive as prose in the same field. // // EMPTY IS VALID AND PERMANENT: a legacy step, for which a renderer falls // back to thought/action. An UNKNOWN non-empty code must render NOTHING — // never the raw token. `STEP_ESCALATED` on a customer's screen is the same // class of defect as `pulse:copywriter` as an agent name, which is what this // whole change exists to end. string code = 12; // The backend-observed facts `code` declares (stepcode.go's // RequiredOperands). Every value already existed in a variable at the call // site: nothing estimated, nothing inferred from elapsed time, nothing read // off the model's own output. // // "Required" is a contract with the CLIENT, not a runtime assertion. A // missing operand must DEGRADE the rendered line, never drop the step — // observability that can break the thing it observes is worse than none. // // Some values are DATA rather than vocabulary: `examples` is quoted model // output, `target` is a caller's URL, `thought` is the model's own words. A // client interpolates those verbatim and never translates them. map<string, string> operands = 13; // How the answer this step reports was produced — mirrors // mesh/telemetry.Provenance, which every recordInference already builds and // which NO card has ever rendered because no AgentStep proto carried it. // // Absent when the step has none. Present-and-fresh is the healthy case and a // renderer is expected to stay silent about it (TIDE's provenance layer: // "silence means measured" — stamping LIVE on every row of a healthy screen // trains the eye to skip the strip). It gets loud on a reused, offline or // degraded answer, which is exactly when a reader needs to know. StepProvenance provenance = 14; } // StepProvenance is the wire copy of mesh/telemetry.Provenance. // // Only the three fields a card can honestly render are carried. `model` is // already AgentStep.model, and `confidence` is omitted because nothing in PULSE // populates it — a chip showing 0.00 would make an unset field look like a // measured score. message StepProvenance { // How it was obtained: "fresh" | "exact-cache" | "near-dup" | "offline". // Unknown values must degrade to "no claim", never render raw. string source = 1; // The cascade rung that produced it, e.g. "full", "exact-cache". Diagnostic // detail for a tooltip; never the primary label. string path = 2; // Produced without full server capability. A reader should weight it lower. bool degraded = 3; // When the underlying value was produced. For a REUSED result this is the // ORIGINAL computation time, which is the whole point: it exposes staleness. // Zero means unknown — not "now". int64 computed_at_unix = 4; } message AgentRun { string run_id = 1; // The recorder's agent id, e.g. "pulse:whitepaper". string agent = 2; string session = 3; int64 started_unix = 4; // Zero while the run is still in flight. int64 ended_unix = 5; AgentRunStatus status = 6; int32 step_count = 7; // Populated only on the initial replay, bounded by replay_steps_per_run. repeated AgentStep steps = 8; string error = 9; } message SubscribeAgentActivityResponse { oneof event { AgentRun snapshot = 1; // Marks the end of the replay. A client renders nothing until it arrives, // so a mid-run subscriber never paints a partial picture and then jumps. bool snapshot_complete = 2; AgentRun run_started = 3; AgentStep step = 4; AgentRun run_finished = 5; } } message ListFeaturedMessagesRequest {} // FeaturedMessage is one operator-curated card in the cockpit's rotating strip: // sponsor and partner copy. // // NOT localized through the app's ARB catalog, unlike the assistant panel's // built-in prompt tips. Sponsor copy is edited against a deployed instance, so // it cannot live in a bundle that requires a rebuild — which is the whole // reason this is an RPC rather than another l10n key. message FeaturedMessage { string id = 1; string title = 2; string body = 3; // BCP-47 tag, e.g. "en", "pt-BR". Empty means "any locale". string locale = 4; // Optional link target. The client decides whether to make the card tappable. string href = 5; // Optional icon hint: a semantic name the client maps to its own icon set, // never a URL, so the card renders with no network fetch and no CSP surface. string icon = 6; } message ListFeaturedMessagesResponse { repeated FeaturedMessage messages = 1; // Where the server read them from, for the operator's benefit when the strip // is unexpectedly empty. Diagnostic only; the client must not parse it. string source = 2; }

data.modelservice#ModelService:
AI model proxy — completion endpoint to the configured local inference engine (mistral.rs’s mistralrs-server).
pulse.v1.ModelService, declared in pulse.proto.
Method Request → Response Least role Notes Complete CompleteRequest → stream StreamChunk editor Complete streams a completion from the configured inference engine. GetModelStatus google.protobuf.Empty → ModelStatus none (public) GetModelStatus returns current model health/readiness. SynthesizeSpeech SynthesizeSpeechRequest → SynthesizeSpeechResponse viewer SynthesizeSpeech turns text into spoken audio and returns the WAV bytes. Synthesis goes through TIDE’s shared ttsd service over HTTP (grpc/internal/speech; endpoint TTSD_URL, unset = the in-cluster Service, empty = voice output disabled -> Unavailable), purpose “readback”. PULSE embeds no TTS engine. TTS_REMOTE_URL, which this comment once named, is read NOWHERE in the server. ConfirmAssistantAction ConfirmAssistantActionRequest → stream AssistantActionEvent editor ConfirmAssistantAction runs a proposal the assistant made in Complete, after the user tapped Confirm. The server re-checks the caller’s role and the stored arguments; an expired, used or someone else’s proposal is refused. Nothing here sends email, posts or calls. Also uses StreamChunk, AssistantToolEvent, AssistantProposal.
message ConfirmAssistantActionRequest { string proposal_id = 1; } message AssistantActionEvent { string status = 1; // running | done string detail = 2; // a progress line from the action, or its result string route = 3; // the page that shows the result string audit_domain = 4; // set when an audit started: the chat shows its progress card string result_id = 5; // id of the record created or changed, when there is one } message SynthesizeSpeechRequest { string text = 1; string voice = 2; // optional voice id; engine default when empty } message SynthesizeSpeechResponse { bytes audio = 1; string format = 2; // e.g. "wav" } message ChatMessage { string role = 1; // "system", "user", "assistant" string content = 2; } message CompleteRequest { string prompt = 1; // simple prompt (use messages for multi-turn) repeated ChatMessage messages = 2; // multi-turn conversation double temperature = 3; double top_p = 4; int32 max_tokens = 5; string agent_id = 6; // which agent profile to use // Variables substituted into the agent's system prompt via Go's // text/template ({{.key}} syntax — see buildAgentSystemPrompt and // agents/templates/*.jinja's default_system_message blocks). Also // differentiates the dedup cache key (see dedupKeyFor) even for agents // whose prompt doesn't reference a given var. map<string, string> template_vars = 7; } message ModelStatus { bool ready = 1; string model_name = 2; int64 context_size = 3; int32 active_requests = 4; double uptime_seconds = 5; string error = 6; }
data.notes#Notes: ModelService is the door to the platform’s own inference plane. There is no third-party model behind it. ActivityService. A subscriber receives only its own runs; a run no account started (a schedule, an inbound message) reaches nobody. Render nothing for an unknown non-empty AgentStep.code, never the raw token; an empty code is valid, so fall back to thought and action. See Agent activity. IdentityService. expires_in is in seconds. Refresh, Google sign-in and sign-out are plain HTTP; see HTTP endpoints.

data: The services behind Brand Analysis: the one-line audit and its stages, the diagnosis, material attached to a new-site audit, content research, market research, Google Search Console, and fixes proposed to the customer’s own website repository. Package pulse.v1; the least role of each method is in its table. See Audit a domain.
data.auditattachmentservice#AuditAttachmentSe:
The material a person gives the new-site audit besides text: photos or a short video of the store or product, product documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD) and voice notes. PULSE audits the brand AGAINST that material: does the site say what the documents and photos show, what is inconsistent, which benefits are not communicated.
UPLOAD IS CHUNKED OVER UNARY RPCS (Begin → Chunk… → Finish) because the web client speaks gRPC-Web, which has no client streaming. Every call is owner scoped: an upload or attachment of another user is NOT_FOUND. Bytes are sealed in PULSE’s appfs root the moment Finish accepts them; nothing is ever written to disk in plaintext. Pass the returned ids in AuditTuning.attachment_ids; an attachment used by a run lives as long as that run, one never used expires (expires_at).
pulse.v1.AuditAttachmentService, declared in attachments.proto.
Method Request → Response Least role Notes GetAttachmentLimits GetAttachmentLimitsRequest → AttachmentLimits viewer What this instance accepts and can understand. Read it before showing the pickers: an instance without a vision tier still accepts photos but says up front that it cannot look at them. BeginAttachmentUpload BeginAttachmentUploadRequest → BeginAttachmentUploadResponse editor Declares a file. Refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT, with a sentence the UI can show) when its type is not accepted or its declared size is over the cap. UploadAttachmentChunk UploadAttachmentChunkRequest → UploadAttachmentChunkResponse editor Appends one chunk at offset (must equal the bytes received so far; a retried chunk at an already-received offset is acknowledged, not duplicated). At most max_chunk_bytes per call. FinishAttachmentUpload FinishAttachmentUploadRequest → AuditAttachment editor Checks the received bytes (size, sha256 when given, real file type, pages/duration caps), seals them and returns the attachment. Extraction then runs in the background: poll GetAttachment until status is not PROCESSING. Documents are usually READY on return. GetAttachment GetAttachmentRequest → AuditAttachment viewer ListAttachments ListAttachmentsRequest → ListAttachmentsResponse viewer DeleteAttachment DeleteAttachmentRequest → DeleteAttachmentResponse editor Removes the sealed bytes and the extracted text. Idempotent. enum AttachmentKind { ATTACHMENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ATTACHMENT_KIND_IMAGE = 1; // jpeg, png, webp ATTACHMENT_KIND_VIDEO = 2; // mp4, webm (short) ATTACHMENT_KIND_DOCUMENT = 3; // pdf, docx, txt, md ATTACHMENT_KIND_AUDIO = 4; // a voice note: wav, webm/ogg opus, m4a, mp3 } enum AttachmentStatus { ATTACHMENT_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ATTACHMENT_STATUS_PROCESSING = 1; // sealed; extraction still running ATTACHMENT_STATUS_READY = 2; // done; see analysis for what was obtained ATTACHMENT_STATUS_FAILED = 3; // stored, but nothing could be read (see detail) } // What PULSE could actually get out of the file. Three of these are honest // "could not" states, never a guess: an image with no vision tier is // IMAGE_UNDERSTANDING_UNAVAILABLE, not a text model's description of a // filename. enum AttachmentAnalysis { ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_PENDING = 1; ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_TEXT_EXTRACTED = 2; // document text read ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_NO_TEXT_FOUND = 3; // read fine, but no text in it (e.g. a scanned PDF) ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_IMAGE_DESCRIBED = 4; // the vision tier described it (video: its frames) ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_IMAGE_UNDERSTANDING_UNAVAILABLE = 5; // no vision tier on this instance, or it did not answer ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_FRAMES_NOT_ANALYSED = 6; // video stored; frames could not be sampled ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_TRANSCRIBED = 7; // voice note transcribed (Voxtral) ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_TRANSCRIPTION_UNAVAILABLE = 8; // no voice tier, or it did not answer ATTACHMENT_ANALYSIS_FAILED = 9; // the file could not be parsed } message GetAttachmentLimitsRequest {} message AttachmentTypeLimit { AttachmentKind kind = 1; repeated string content_types = 2; // accepted MIME types repeated string extensions = 3; // accepted extensions, lower case, no dot int64 max_bytes = 4; int32 max_duration_seconds = 5; // video/audio; 0 = not applicable int32 max_pages = 6; // documents; 0 = not applicable } message AttachmentLimits { repeated AttachmentTypeLimit types = 1; int32 max_attachments_per_audit = 2; int32 max_chunk_bytes = 3; // Whether the instance can look inside the material, decided from its // configuration (a vision tier, a voice tier, a frame sampler). False is // shown to the person before they upload. bool image_understanding_available = 4; bool transcription_available = 5; bool video_frames_available = 6; int32 unused_retention_hours = 7; // an attachment no run used is removed after this } message BeginAttachmentUploadRequest { string filename = 1; // shown back and cited in findings; path parts are dropped string content_type = 2; // as the picker reports it; the bytes are checked at Finish int64 size_bytes = 3; // declared total size; Finish refuses a different count } message BeginAttachmentUploadResponse { string upload_id = 1; AttachmentKind kind = 2; int32 max_chunk_bytes = 3; google.protobuf.Timestamp expires_at = 4; // an unfinished upload is dropped after this } message UploadAttachmentChunkRequest { string upload_id = 1; int64 offset = 2; bytes data = 3; } message UploadAttachmentChunkResponse { int64 received_bytes = 1; } message FinishAttachmentUploadRequest { string upload_id = 1; string sha256_hex = 2; // optional; checked when set } message AuditAttachment { string id = 1; string filename = 2; string content_type = 3; // as detected from the bytes AttachmentKind kind = 4; int64 size_bytes = 5; AttachmentStatus status = 6; AttachmentAnalysis analysis = 7; string detail = 8; // one sentence for the person: what was read, or why not string summary = 9; // first part of what was extracted/described (bounded) int32 extracted_chars = 10; // size of the full extracted text the audit can use int32 page_count = 11; // documents; 0 = unknown int32 duration_seconds = 12; // video/audio; 0 = unknown int32 frames_analysed = 13; // video string audit_run_id = 14; // the run that used it; "" = not used yet google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 15; google.protobuf.Timestamp expires_at = 16; // unset once a run uses it // What the audit run (audit_run_id) found comparing the site with this // material, each judged by the plan gate. Empty until that run's diagnosis. repeated AttachmentFinding findings = 17; } // One brand-vs-material finding drawn from an attachment. message AttachmentFinding { string type = 1; // gap | inconsistency | uncommunicated_benefit | confirmed string finding = 2; // one sentence string action = 3; // what to change on the site or in marketing string judgement = 4; // the plan gate's verdict text; "" = not judged (PULSE_JUDGEMENT=off) } message GetAttachmentRequest { string attachment_id = 1; } message ListAttachmentsRequest { string audit_run_id = 1; // optional: only those a run used } message ListAttachmentsResponse { repeated AuditAttachment attachments = 1; } message DeleteAttachmentRequest { string attachment_id = 1; } message DeleteAttachmentResponse { bool deleted = 1; // false when there was nothing to delete }
data.insightsservice#InsightsService:
Prescriptive content intelligence — the analysis behind the Content Gaps, Content Strategy, and Strategy Roadmap surfaces. Each RPC is synthesized by the platform’s OWN sovereign model (no external AI), grounded in the user’s diagnosis + published content + live market signals, and returned as structured rows the limbic screens render directly (plus a summary and a single headline score).
pulse.v1.InsightsService, declared in pulse.proto.
Method Request → Response Least role Notes AnalyzeContentGaps AnalyzeContentGapsRequest → ContentGapsResponse editor AnalyzeContentGaps finds topics/formats the user under-serves vs. demand. GenerateContentStrategy GenerateContentStrategyRequest → ContentStrategyResponse editor GenerateContentStrategy proposes content pillars, cadence, and themes. GenerateStrategyRoadmap GenerateStrategyRoadmapRequest → StrategyRoadmapResponse editor GenerateStrategyRoadmap lays out a phased go-to-market roadmap. GetAuditContentGaps GetAuditContentGapsRequest → AuditContentGaps viewer GetAuditContentGaps returns the content gaps computed after the caller’s latest audit, and that step’s progress. No model call. ListOwnInsights ListOwnInsightsRequest → ListOwnInsightsResponse viewer ListOwnInsights lists what the caller ran by hand (AnalyzeContentGaps, GenerateContentStrategy), newest first, as stored. No model call. Also uses DateRange, Channel.
message GetAuditContentGapsRequest {} message ListOwnInsightsRequest {} // One result the user ran by hand; exactly one of gaps / strategy is set. message OwnInsight { string id = 1; string kind = 2; // content_gaps | content_strategy google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 3; ContentGapsResponse gaps = 4; ContentStrategyResponse strategy = 5; } message ListOwnInsightsResponse { repeated OwnInsight insights = 1; } message AuditContentGaps { // Unset when no audit has computed gaps yet. ContentGapsResponse gaps = 1; // The latest audit run ("" = the caller never ran one) and its domain. string audit_run_id = 2; string domain = 3; // That run's content_gaps stage: pending | running | done | failed | // skipped ("" = no run), and its detail or error. string stage_status = 4; string stage_detail = 5; // The run whose gaps are shown, when it is an earlier one than audit_run_id. string gaps_audit_run_id = 6; // The campaign PULSE proposed from these gaps ("" = none). string campaign_id = 7; // Gaps that serve nothing the business sells (offering_match = no_match): // kept out of gaps, offered as "doesn't match what you sell". repeated ContentGap unmatched_gaps = 8; } message AnalyzeContentGapsRequest { string focus_area = 1; // optional theme to concentrate the analysis on DateRange date_range = 2; // window of published content to assess // A competitor to compare with: its site (example.com) or a social handle // (@name). A site is read; a handle is named only. "" = none. string competitor = 3; } message ContentGap { string topic = 1; string format = 2; // e.g. "article", "video", "infographic" double demand_score = 3; // 0-100 — how much the audience wants this double coverage_score = 4; // 0-100 — how well the user currently covers it double opportunity = 5; // 0-100 — prescriptive priority (demand vs coverage) string rationale = 6; // The judging ladder's verdict on this gap (cmd/judgement_gate.go): concur or // unable-to-judge only — a dissented gap is withheld and appears only in // ContentGapsResponse.judgements. Unset = judging off (PULSE_JUDGEMENT=off). runink.ui.judgement.v1.Judgement judgement = 7; // The audit findings this gap was drawn from. Empty = it cites none (the // analysis was not run on an audit, or the model cited nothing that exists). repeated GapEvidence evidence = 8; // What the business sells that this gap serves, as the site or the owner // states it ("" = none matched). string offering = 9; // matches | no_match | not_checked (no offerings were known). string offering_match = 10; } // One audit finding a gap cites. The three scores of a gap are the model's // estimates; evidence is what the audit measured. message GapEvidence { string ref = 1; // "E3" string kind = 2; // site_score | check | discover | retention | trend | ai_visibility string text = 3; string source_url = 4; // "" when the finding has no page of its own } message ContentGapsResponse { repeated ContentGap gaps = 1; double coverage_index = 2; // headline: overall content coverage 0-100 string summary = 3; google.protobuf.Timestamp generated_at = 4; // Every verdict of this run, accepted AND rejected, with the ladder's counts. runink.ui.judgement.v1.JudgementSet judgements = 5; // What the check was asked (a manual check; "" = not asked). string focus_area = 6; string competitor = 7; // How the competitor was used: "read" (its site's text was read) | // "handle" (named only: a handle has no page PULSE reads) | "unreadable" // (its site could not be read; competitor_reason says why) | "" (none). string competitor_read = 8; string competitor_reason = 9; // How many of the latest audit's measured findings the check was given // (0 = no audit to cite). int32 audit_evidence_count = 10; data.notes#Notes: One deadline. GenerateDiagnostic and a score-only RunAudit run under one end-to-end budget, PULSE_AUDIT_DEADLINE_SECONDS (170 seconds by default). Each phase gets a budget from what is left; a phase that does not finish is named on the result as not completed within the budget, and the diagnosis is returned as a partial result rather than discarded. Judged output. Diagnostic.channel_prescriptions and brand_visibility hold only proposals the judging ladder kept; judgements lists every verdict. Audit runs. RunAudit runs the stages detached from the call (bounded at 45 minutes), resumes from the first stage not done, reuses a run from the last 24 hours unless force is set, and attaches to a run already in flight. score_only runs just normalize and score on the URL as given; an identical score-only run within PULSE_AUDIT_CACHE_TTL (one hour by default) is reused unless force. Read the report with GetAuditRun (AuditRun.score_report). Stages. stage is a stable identifier: show it as-is or map it to your own labels, but do not rely on the set of stages or their order. A stage that could not run because an earlier one did not finish is skipped, with an error that starts blocked:. queue_position is set while a stage waits for model capacity. The terminal event has an empty stage and the run’s final run_status. With TIDE_HEALTH_URL set, each stage reports to agent health as pulse-audit-. Stored reads. The Radar List* methods read what earlier research and audits persisted; they search nothing and spend no model time. Guest opportunities found by Radar are saved onto Influencers, scored by topical relevance, never by an audience figure. Changing a site. ApplyAuditActions modes other than plan need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true, PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true and an admin; every mode needs repo_path inside PULSE_APPLY_ROOT. SiteRepoService.ProposeSiteFix needs the same two switches and an admin, writes only to a new pulse/- branch and opens a pull request. ConnectSiteRepo and DisconnectSiteRepo also check for an admin, although their table role is editor. See Website repository. Search Console. StartSearchConsoleConnect returns Google’s consent address; Google returns to /oauth/search-console/callback. Without the Google OAuth client or an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL the answer says what is not set up. See Google.

Google Analytics (GA4) trend data + Prophet-style forecasting. SyncGaData pulls a metric’s daily time series from the configured GA4 property (see IntegrationService for how the service-account credential is stored) into the local ga_metrics cache. data.automationservice#AutomationService:
AutomationService — Content › Automations: a person’s marketing automations, each ONE trigger and a graph of steps, drawn on the shared flow studio (org-runink/ui flow). The engine is ui’s flow/engine; every step calls an existing PULSE capability with the AUTOMATION OWNER’s identity and RBAC.
The rules a reader can rely on: * The model PROPOSES; the person APPROVES. The assistant’s propose_automation tool never changes an automation: it stores a pending proposal (plan-gated). data.autopilotservice#AutopilotService:
AutopilotService — PULSE runs a connected social account by itself AFTER a person approves the content (owner, 2026-10-29: “PULSE agents will autonomously manage our social media accounts once the content is approved”).
The rules a reader can rely on: * Approval is the human gate. Autopilot schedules only content a person approved, and the publishing worker checks the approval again on the row it is about to send. * PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and the per-channel PULSE_PUBLISH_(channel) switches are the hard kill switches: autopilot never schedules on a disarmed channel and every send passes the same dispatch gate as a manual one. * An account pauses by itself on an expired connection, a rate limit or repeated failures, and says so in To do today with a reconnect link. * Replies to comments are drafted into an approval queue. Auto-reply is OFF by default and, when a person turns it on, covers only thanks, an answer from approved FAQ content and a link to the business’s own site; each auto-reply passes OpenBias and the plan gate and is logged. * Comments, mentions, DMs and results are read only where the connector provides them; elsewhere the account says PULSE cannot read them yet. * Everything is owner-scoped.

SERVICE: EpicService — Epics and Milestones (replaces the Strategy Roadmap) An epic is one campaign objective with a measured KPI, an accountable owner (who created it), a named approver and RACI. A milestone is a dated gate with an exit threshold on that KPI and a Definition of Done; the campaign’s roadmap items roll up into milestones. Every figure (KPI, forecast, control chart, schedule index) is computed in Go from stored measurements; a figure that cannot be computed is unset with the reason, never 0.

data.notes#Notes: Measured only. Metrics come from connected sources: Google Analytics 4 as channel web, Google Ads as google_ads, Google Search Console clicks and impressions, and the leads PULSE holds. Published posts have their own results, read back into post_results. A channel with no connector has no rows. A figure is counted only when measured_fields names it; measured_days of 0 means nothing was measured. Nothing writes follower counts. Forecasts. GetForecast splits the cached Google Analytics series into trend, seasonality and changepoints and extends it, without a live Google call and without model inference. season_period_days is 0 when no seasonality was found. Autopilot queues approved posts at the account’s best time through the same publishing gate as any scheduled post, so the switches on Switches and arming order still decide at send time. Replies drafted from read-back comments wait in the approval queue. Automations do outbound work only with PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS and each step’s own channel switch; a dry run never sends. Campaign plans. Go lays out the calendar from the person’s capacity and dates; the campaign-plan skill fills the posts; checks reject plans over capacity or with missing fields. KPI results come only from post_results.

data.notes#Notes: Our own model only. Everything here generates on the platform’s own inference plane through the model router. There is no image-generation tier: GenerateCreative for a still image answers Unimplemented. Skills run as one bounded pipeline: OpenBias on the inputs, the prompt, TOON output, Go checks, one revision only when a check failed, OpenBias on the draft, then the plan gate. Drafts land on the board with their scores in content.metadata. Publishing queue. status is pending, publishing, posted, withheld or failed. reason_status is recorded, none, missing or unavailable: never read an empty reason as “nothing to report” without checking it. Speech comes from TIDE’s shared ttsd (TTSD_URL). When it is switched off, a method that needs speech answers Unavailable rather than silence.

Besides gRPC and gRPC-Web, the backend answers a short, fixed list of plain HTTP routes on the same port. None of them is a data API. Campaigns, content, leads, and everything else are gRPC only.
Route Auth Purpose GET /health None Always 200. Body: {"status":"ok","model_ready":<bool>,"port":<int>} GET /auth/config None {"google_client_id":"…","password_auth":<bool>} for the login screen POST /auth/google None (it is the sign-in) Exchanges a Google ID token for a PULSE session. Same JSON shape as Login. With x-pulse-session: cookie it sets the session cookie and returns no token. POST /auth/refresh Refresh token Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair in the same session. Refused once the session is signed out. POST /auth/logout The session cookie Revokes the browser session and clears the cookie. It clears the cookie even when the session has already expired, which is how a stale one is cleaned up. /creatives/<name>, /media/<name> The owner’s session, or a server-signed URL Generated media, decrypted from the sealed store GET /podcast/feed.xml None, on purpose The podcast RSS feed that podcast platforms poll. Needs PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. POST /voice/webrtc/offer Session Forwards a WebRTC offer to the calling agent (CALLING_AGENT_URL). 503 when that is not set. POST /voice/transcribe Session Raw PCM in, {"text":"…"} out, via Voxtral GET /.well-known/agent-card.json None The A2A agent card /a2a Session (bearer header only) A2A JSON-RPC. See Calling the API. POST /twilio/message Twilio signature Inbound WhatsApp and SMS POST /inbound/leads/<secret> (and OPTIONS) The secret in the path; no session, no cookie A website enquiry becomes a lead. Form-encoded, multipart or JSON, at most 16 KiB. CORS only for the sites listed on the link. Served ahead of every other route, including gRPC-Web and the deployment-wide CORS headers. See Website form. POST /comms/twilio/status Twilio signature Delivery-status callbacks for messages and calls sent from the Send / Call panel. An unsigned callback is refused and changes nothing. POST /comms/twilio/inbound Twilio signature Replies to PULSE’s SMS sender: STOP and START (and their synonyms) are recorded for the number; other replies are not stored. Refuses everything (503) while no Twilio auth token is set. POST /pulse/aicall/twilio/answer, POST /pulse/aicall/twilio/status Twilio signature An AI call’s answer (a person gets the disclosure and the conversation, a voicemail the short message) and its final status. /pulse/aicall/twilio/stream/<token> A single-use token minted by the signed answer The AI call’s audio over a WebSocket. GET /oauth/mail/callback The single-use state from the connect link Google or Microsoft returns here after Connect Gmail or Connect Microsoft 365. GET /oauth/social/callback The single-use state from StartSocialConnect Meta, Google or LinkedIn returns here after Connect with Instagram, YouTube or LinkedIn; the tokens are sealed and the window shows the result. GET /oauth/search-console/callback The single-use state from StartSearchConsoleConnect Google returns here after Connect Search Console. anything else None The Flutter web app, when PULSE_WEB_DIR is set Requests with gRPC-Web content types go to the gRPC server before any of these routes are checked. A route in the table above is matched before the web app’s catch-all, so the app never answers one of them with its own page.
The three /oauth/…/callback routes are what you register as redirect URIs in each developer console, under PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. The social and Search Console sign-ins are offered only when that address is https. The TIDE edge must route them to the backend. See Public address and redirects.

data.agencyservice#AgencyService:
AgencyService — one agency runs several client businesses in PULSE. Each client is its own owner: its brand, accounts, autopilot, approvals and reports are the client’s rows, and every owner-scoped query keeps them apart. The app picks the client with the x-pulse-client request header; the server checks the caller’s membership on every call.
Roles per client: agency_admin (runs everything for the client, adds people) and client_approver (sees the client’s work and approves or rejects content and replies — nothing else).

data.aicallservice#AICallService:
AICallService places AI voice calls to leads (an AI assistant talks to the lead over Twilio, through org-runink/ui comms/voiceagent) and keeps the records those calls need: the lead’s prior express consent, the lead’s time zone, the tenant’s do-not-call list, each call’s outcome and sealed transcript, and the follow-up task a call leaves behind.
SERVER-SIDE GUARDS (PlaceAICall refuses, with every reason, unless all hold): - PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true, PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS and PULSE_AI_CALLS on; - the caller is an editor or admin (read from the users row); - the lead’s phone has a consent record (who recorded it, when and how it was given) for THAT number, not revoked — an AI voice is an artificial voice under the TCPA (FCC, February 2024); - the number is not on the tenant’s do-not-call list; - the lead’s local time (its time zone is required) is inside the calling-hours window, itself inside 08:00–21:00; - fewer than max_attempts AI calls to the lead in the last 30 days, and none in progress; - the tenant’s Twilio caller ID is configured (the call is placed from it). Every call opens with “an AI assistant calling on behalf of” and the company, then the recording notice; “stop” / “do not call” on a call puts the number on the do-not-call list.
Automations call PlaceAICall as a step with origin “automation:” plus the automation id; a refusal is a result (placed=false, refusals), not an RPC error.

Required. string evidence = 3; google.protobuf.Timestamp given_at = 4; // when the lead gave it; not in the future } message RevokeCallConsentRequest { string lead_id = 1; } message SetLeadTimeZoneRequest { string lead_id = 1; string time_zone = 2; // IANA, e.g. "America/New_York" } message DoNotCallEntry { string id = 1; string number_masked = 2; string reason = 3; string source = 4; // "call" (said on a call) | "manual" google.protobuf.Timestamp added_at = 5; string added_by = 6; // user id, or "call:" plus the call id } message ListDoNotCallRequest {} message ListDoNotCallResponse { repeated DoNotCallEntry entries = 1; } message AddDoNotCallRequest { string lead_id = 1; string reason = 2; } message FollowUpTask { string id = 1; string lead_id = 2; string title = 3; string detail = 4; google.protobuf.Timestamp due_at = 5; string status = 6; // "open" | "done" string source_call_id = 7; google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 8; } message ListLeadFollowUpsRequest { string lead_id = 1; } message ListLeadFollowUpsResponse { repeated FollowUpTask tasks = 1; }

data.notes#Notes: Integrations are the caller’s own rows, so reading them is open to a viewer and changing them needs an editor, not an admin. HubSpot and GitHub connections go through the shared ConnectionsService instead; see Shared components. Sign-in connections. StartSocialConnect returns the consent address for instagram, youtube or linkedin (company_pages adds the LinkedIn page scopes when LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES is on). The platform returns to /oauth/social/callback, which seals the tokens. The answer is configured=false with a message when the server has no app client or no https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. ListSocialConnections reports one status per platform and, per feature, the permissions needed and granted. DisconnectSocial revokes the grant at the platform where its API allows, then deletes the sealed tokens. See Setup. Outbound. SendOutreachEmail needs PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL armed and a connected mailbox; CallLead needs PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS; AICallService.PlaceAICall needs PULSE_AI_CALLS and the lead’s recorded consent. See Switches and arming order. Agencies. A client is its own owner id. Sending x-pulse-client with a client the caller is a member of makes that client the caller. Opportunities are read from open procurement data; nothing is sent or submitted.
data.opportunityservice#OpportunityService:
OpportunityService — Audience › Opportunities (owner, 2026-10-30): public tenders and private requests for proposals that need what the account sells (websites, custom applications, content …), and a drafted response.
The rules a reader can rely on: * Sources are official open procurement data (EU TED, UK Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, Brazil PNCP, CanadaBuys; US SAM.gov with the account’s own key from Integrations) plus private requests for proposals PULSE’s own crawler finds. No login is scraped. * Each source reports read (with a count), empty, unreadable (with the reason) or not connected. A source that could not be read is never shown as having nothing. * A figure a notice does not state (value, deadline) is absent, never 0. * Matching is the account’s offerings (audit + tuning) mapped to procurement codes (CPV, UNSPSC, NAICS) plus lexical word matching (no embeddings); every card says why it matched. * A drafted response is a draft: nothing here submits anywhere. The person submits, and records it by moving the card to Submitted.

data:
Four ideas explain almost everything you see in Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine.
Measured and not measuredWhy PULSE shows “Not measured” instead of a 0 or a guess. The plan gateThe model proposes; a reviewer checks it against the evidence before it is kept. Drafts, approval and publishingHow a post goes from an idea to sent, and every switch on the way. PersonasWho you talk to, taken from your check-up and your leads, never invented. In one paragraph. PULSE measures what it can (your site, the web, the accounts you connect, its own records), says plainly what it could not measure, and proposes work from that: a plan, campaigns, posts, replies, leads. Every proposal is checked, by rules and by a reviewer, before you see it. Nothing leaves PULSE until you approve it, and not even then unless your administrator has switched publishing on.
data.for-administrators-and-developers#For ad: How PULSE is builtOne process, one port, the call chain, and where data lives. Sovereign inferenceOne shared model server, time budgets, and grounding. Agent activityThe live feed of what every agent is doing.

data: A long generation can hold the inference server for minutes. Without a shared view, it is visible only on the screen that started it. The agent activity card fixes that. It is fed by ActivityService.SubscribeAgentActivity.
data.opening-the-page-mid-run#Opening the pag: When you subscribe, the server first replays every run in progress, with the steps recorded so far. Then it sends snapshot_complete, and after that live events. So a page opened halfway through a run still shows that run.
data.the-featured-strip#The featured strip: ActivityService.ListFeaturedMessages returns operator-written sponsor and partner cards for the rotating strip. The server reads them from a file named by FEATURED_MESSAGES_PATH. When that is unset, it looks for a file named featured_messages.json in /app, the working directory, data, and /app/data, in that order. No file means an empty strip, not an error. You can change the cards without rebuilding the app.
data.what-you-see#What you see:
Each run shows its agent (for example pulse:whitepaper), its status (running, done, or failed), and its steps.
A step is not a sentence the backend wrote. PULSE emits a code from the reasoning-step vocabulary shared with the rest of the Runink platform, plus the operands that go with it, and the client composes the line in your language. The codes PULSE emits say that a prompt was dispatched (with the model and the token ceiling it was dispatched with), that a source is about to be read or was read or could not be read, that tokens are coming back (count and elapsed time, marked approximate because a stream does not promise one frame per token), that a draft was rewritten or a reply refused, what was found, and that the run finished or failed. A step the client has no line for renders as nothing rather than as an internal token.
Every operand is a value the backend already held. Nothing is estimated from elapsed time or read off the model’s own account of itself, and a measurement that is missing is left out rather than sent as a zero — an unknown token count is not a cheap generation.
A step can also carry provenance: whether the answer is fresh or reused from a cache, and whether it was produced in a degraded mode. A healthy, fresh answer shows nothing extra. The card calls out only reused, offline, or degraded answers.
PULSE does not run a propose-then-critique loop, so a plain generation is a short sequence of these steps. Longer pieces of work have more: the one-phrase audit runs tracked stages, and each stage also reports its own health to the operator console as its own agent, so a stage that wedges goes stale there instead of disappearing.
data.whose-runs-you-see#Whose runs you see:
By default you see your own session’s runs. The server uses the session field of the request, or, when that is empty, the caller’s x-agent-trace-id header.
Work started without a request behind it (a schedule, a WhatsApp message, an A2A call, a background engine) has no session. A scoped subscriber does not see those runs. Only a subscriber that sends neither a session nor a trace ID gets the ambient view of everything. An operator console does that on purpose.

data:
Every post PULSE prepares goes the same way, and you can follow it on its step trail:
Planned → Drafted → Approved → Scheduled → Sent, or Withheld, Failed or Missed.
data.1-planned#1. Planned: A campaign’s plan, or your check-up, holds the idea of a post: its topic, format, who it is for and when. It sits in the Planned column of Campaigns. It is not written yet, so it cannot be approved or scheduled.
data.2-drafted#2. Drafted: PULSE writes it, from the plan, from your check-up, from a campaign’s daily drafts, or because you asked in Studio. The draft is checked (the skill’s checks, PULSE’s safety rules, the plan gate) and lands in Drafts to approve. Nothing is posted at this stage.
data.3-approved#3. Approved: You approve it, on the Campaigns board, in Studio, or through the assistant (which asks you to confirm). Only an editor or admin can approve. Approval is the only way a post moves on: PULSE never publishes a piece nobody approved.
data.4-scheduled#4. Scheduled:
An approved post gets a time:
the time you pick when you move it to Scheduled; its planned time, if it already had one still ahead; with Autopilot on for that account, the account’s best time (never before the post’s planned time); with Autopilot off and no time, it goes out at once. A post whose time passes while it still waits for approval is Missed. It is never sent late; reschedule it.
data.5-sent-or-held-back#5. Sent, or held bac:
When the time comes, PULSE checks, in that moment, everything that must agree:
Check Who controls it The channel is one PULSE can post to PULSE: Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, your website’s blog, the podcast and audiobook feed The account is connected You, in Settings → Integrations The channel is Active You, on its card Publishing is switched on for the whole PULSE (the kill switch) Your administrator Publishing is switched on for that channel Your administrator For LinkedIn, the blog, the podcast and the audiobook: you are one of the named publishers Your administrator If all agree, the post goes out and moves to Sent, with its link where the platform gives one. If one does not, the post is Withheld (held back) with the reason, or Failed with the platform’s reason. A withheld post is never sent later on its own: fix the cause and schedule it again.
The Integrations card of each channel tells you in advance whether it can publish (Ready to publish, or Can’t publish: and why), so you do not have to wait for a post to be held back to find out.
data.posting-it-yourself#Posting it yourself: Any approved, scheduled or sent piece can be downloaded as files you post yourself: the picture or video, and the caption. That is the way for Facebook, X, email newsletters, or any channel you have not connected. See Download.
data.replies#Replies:
Replies to comments, mentions and messages follow the same rule: drafted, waiting for you under Replies waiting for you, sent only when you send them, and only through a channel whose switches allow replies. The one exception you can turn on is answering simple comments by itself, limited to three kinds of reply, each checked first.
For administrators, every switch, its default and the safe order to turn them on: Switches and arming order.

data:
For administrators and developers. PULSE is application code only: a Go gRPC backend (grpc/) and a Flutter client (flutter/) for web, Linux and Android. The platform around it lives in other Runink repositories:
Runink TIDE runs the local dev loop (tide dev), the deploys, the operator that reconciles a PULSE instance (in the pulse-system namespace), the image builds and the shared model weights. The libraries security, mesh, inference, store, crawler, billing and ui supply authentication and sealing, interceptors and self-healing, the inference wrappers and the plan gate, persistence, headless web research, metering, and the shared pages (Billing, Profile, Admin, Data sources).
data.ai#AI: All AI runs on the platform’s own inference server (mistral.rs); PULSE calls no outside AI service and keeps no embeddings or vector index. See Sovereign inference. What a model proposes passes the plan gate before it is kept.
data.every-call-goes-through-the-same-chain#E: gRPC calls pass through the same interceptors in the same order: panic recovery, optional per-caller rate limiting (off unless PULSE_RATE_RPS is set), request logging, then authentication and authorization. Every method needs a valid session except sign-in and the model status; the caller’s role is checked against each method. Streaming calls also get serialized sends and a heartbeat, which keeps long generations alive through proxies.
data.one-process-one-port#One process, one po:
pulse-server serve is one Go process listening on one port. A multiplexer splits that port in two:
Connections with content-type: application/grpc go to the gRPC server. Everything else goes to an HTTP handler: gRPC-Web for browsers, /health, generated media, the voice endpoints, the sign-in and OAuth callbacks, the podcast feed, the website-form endpoint, and, when PULSE_WEB_DIR is set, the Flutter web build itself. When the backend serves the web build, the app and the API share an origin and browsers make no CORS requests. Every HTTP endpoint is listed in the API reference; every gRPC service in the API reference.
data.where-data-lives#Where data lives: SQLite holds the business data. In a cluster, Litestream replicates it to the in-cluster object store. SQLite has one writer, so a deployment runs one backend instance. Tokens and passwords of connected accounts are sealed, column by column, before they are written (TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK is required). The app root holds sessions, generated media and the memo cache, each sealed. The server does not start if it cannot mount it. Configuration, switches and operations are in the Admin guide; building and calling the API in the Developer guide.

data: PULSE shows a figure only when something measured it. A figure nobody measured is not drawn as 0 and is not estimated: it says Not measured, or shows —. A 0 is a real answer (“we looked and there were none”); “not measured” means nobody looked.
data.lines-over-time#Lines over time: A line is drawn only through measured points, and starts once there are two. A day or a check-up that measured nothing is a gap, not a 0.
data.the-answers-you-will-see#The answers you: What the app says What it means A figure A source answered: your site, the web, a platform, a connected account, or PULSE’s own records. Counted From PULSE’s own records (posts sent, drafts approved, tasks done). A 0 here is a real 0. Nothing found / None in the last 28 days The source answered and had nothing. Not measured / — No source answered. No figure is shown. Needs a connection / Connect … Only an account you have not connected can answer it. Could not be read The source exists but did not answer right now, usually with the reason. Try again later. Not recorded It happened, but PULSE kept no record of it. not yet It has not happened. Three of these are easy to confuse, and the app keeps them apart on purpose: an empty answer, no answer, and an answer that could not be read. A page that could not read something says so rather than showing an empty list.
data.when-the-model-estimates#When the model:
Some numbers are the model’s judgement, not a measurement. The app labels them as such, for example a trending topic’s heat … (model estimate) or a content gap’s demand and opportunity scores. A lead’s fit tier (high, medium, low) is read from what its record holds and is not a probability.
The model never writes a performance figure. In a report, the figures are written by PULSE from your measured records, and any sentence of the model’s that names a figure not in those records is removed. See Reports.
data.where-the-figures-come-from#Where the fi: Source Examples Your check-up Site score, AI and search visibility, Google Discover readiness, leads, competitors, partners PULSE’s own records What PULSE did: posts sent, drafts approved, outreach drafted, tasks done The platforms Each post’s results as Instagram, LinkedIn or YouTube report them Accounts you connect Google Analytics, Google Ads, Google Search Console You Your weekly check-ins, deal values A figure a platform does not report for a kind of post is “not measured” for that post, never 0.

data: A persona is a kind of customer you talk to, such as “wedding planners” or “owners of small gyms”. PULSE uses personas to decide who each post and each content idea is for, and in what tone. PULSE never invents a persona: each one comes from something you said or something PULSE found, and says where it came from.
data.when-there-are-none#When there are none:
With no check-up and no leads, PULSE does not know who you talk to, and it says so instead of guessing. A campaign plan is then refused with: PULSE does not know who you talk to yet: run a site audit (it asks who buys from you) or add leads, then plan again.
To give PULSE better personas, answer Who usually buys from you? in your check-up, set who you sell to under Fine-tune the content ideas, and keep your leads’ job titles filled in.
The separate Persona Profile page left PULSE; its old addresses (/persona-profile, /customer360, /intelligence-console) open Leads.
data.where-personas-come-from#Where personas:
In this order, with duplicates removed and at most five kept:
The campaign’s audience, when the campaign names one. Who buys from you, from your check-up: your answer to “Who usually buys from you?”, or what the check-up found. The audience segments in your check-up’s diagnosis. Your leads’ job titles: a title that at least two of your leads share (the two most common). The personas of your content ideas, which themselves come from what you told PULSE, your leads, or the diagnosis’s audience.
data.where-they-are-used#Where they are used: Campaign plans: each planned post is for one persona, written exactly as above, and the plan gives each persona a tone (three adjectives and an example line). The plan’s checks flag any post written for someone who is not on the list. You see the persona on each planned post as “For: …”. Content ideas: each idea is for one persona, with one problem and one angle. See Ideas for what to post.

data:
The model proposes; the plan gate judges. Before PULSE keeps something its model proposed, a second pass, PULSE’s reviewer, checks it against the evidence that run actually gathered: the pages read, the web research, your connected accounts’ figures, your check-up. The app calls it “PULSE’s reviewer”; these docs call it the plan gate.
The reviewer runs on the same model server, with its own instructions and at a near-zero temperature, so the same evidence gets the same verdict.
data.for-administrators#For administrators: The gate is on by default. PULSE_JUDGEMENT=off turns it off: proposals then pass unjudged and the app says the reviewer is switched off. A verdict the model wrote into its own proposal is removed before judging; the reviewer is the only source of a verdict. In the API, judged messages carry a judgement field and responses a judgements set listing every verdict, kept or withheld (accepted=false). See Common types and Configuration.
data.what-the-verdict-does#What the verdict d: Verdict In the app Effect Agreed “The reviewer agreed with it.” Kept. Could not judge “The reviewer could not check it, so it is not approved by the reviewer.” Kept, and marked. It is never shown as agreement. Disagreed Withheld / held back, with the reason Not kept. It is listed as withheld, never shown as a proposal. Switched off “The reviewer is switched off on this server.” Kept without review, and marked. “Could not judge” covers every case where no verdict was reached: nothing to judge against, no model available, or no answer in time.
data.where-you-meet-it#Where you meet it: Your check-up: the plan in the diagnosis, and the New groups of customers to try (withheld ones are not shown). Content ideas: ideas that do not pass are listed as held back, with the reason. Studio drafts written by a skill: the verdict is shown under What PULSE checked. Campaign plans: “PULSE’s reviewer checked this plan against your audit”, or why it could not. Site fixes: a pull request the reviewer does not agree with says Withheld by the plan gate, and nothing is opened. Autopilot replies: a reply goes out by itself only when PULSE’s safety rules and the reviewer both agree; otherwise it waits for you. Automations the assistant proposes and AI calls. The plan gate is one check among several. Skills also run their own rule checks (see The checks), and PULSE’s safety rules screen inputs and drafts. None of them publishes anything: that still needs your approval and the publishing switches.

data: Every AI feature in PULSE runs on the Runink platform’s own inference server: mistral.rs’s mistralrs-server. PULSE sends no prompt, no customer data, and no generated text to any third-party model API.
data.grounding#Grounding:
Generators ground their output in real sources before they write:
Web research. A headless Chrome scraper and extractor reads live pages and search results. The diagnosis reads your website this way. Product facts. Plain markdown files shipped in the image (grpc/data/corpus), read by Direct Corpus Interaction. The topic’s terms are grepped across the corpus, the files that matched are read whole, and the passages carrying the most distinct terms go into the prompt labelled with the file they came from. There are no embeddings, no vector index, and no similarity search anywhere in PULSE. Files whose name begins with _ are rules: they are injected verbatim into every long-form generation, matched or not, because a lookup by relevance would never return them. When nothing matches, the generator is told so in as many words and writes from the brief alone, rather than filling the gap.
data.is-the-model-ready#Is the model ready:
Two signals report readiness, and both use the same test: the engine process is running, and a readiness check against the engine has confirmed it can serve a request.
GET /health returns model_ready. ModelService/GetModelStatus returns ready. The app polls it on startup. A process that has started but is still loading weights counts as not ready.
data.one-server-for-everything#One server for:
All AI services share one inference server and one model server object inside PULSE, so they share one set of agent prompts and parameters (agents/pulse.ini and the templates in agents/templates/).
The backend finds the server one of two ways:
Remote. When INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL is set, PULSE uses the shared inference plane at that address and starts nothing itself. Local. Otherwise it starts mistralrs-server as a child process. Speech-to-text works the same way with its own variable, VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL, and its own mistralrs-server serving Voxtral. Text-to-speech is Runink TIDE’s shared ttsd service, reached through TTSD_URL (unset: the in-cluster Service; empty: voice output off). PULSE embeds no speech engine.
Both servers start in the background. If a binary or model is missing, PULSE still starts, and AI calls fail with inference server is not running instead of blocking the whole app.
data.output-guards#Output guards: Everything PULSE can publish is screened before it reaches you, and nothing is published without a person’s approval. Operators can widen screening in Configuration; screening buffers the whole response, so a screened answer arrives at once rather than token by token.
data.repeat-requests#Repeat requests: An exact repeat of a content generation is served from a cache instead of running the model again. PULSE_DEDUP_TTL sets how long an entry lives, as a Go duration. The default is 1h.
data.sharing-the-slot-fairly#Sharing the slot:
Optional admission control queues or refuses work when the model is busy. It is off unless PULSE_ADMIT_MAX is above zero.
Variable Meaning PULSE_ADMIT_MAX Maximum concurrent inference calls. 0 turns admission off. PULSE_ADMIT_QUEUE Maximum waiters before backpressure. 0 is unbounded. PULSE_ADMIT_MODE reject (default) or degrade. PULSE_ADMIT_WEIGHTS Scheduling weights keyed by the x-subscription-tier request metadata, for example enterprise:4,dedicated:4,lite:1. A request without that metadata is scheduled as default. When the pool is full in reject mode, the caller gets ResourceExhausted: the inference plane is at capacity and declined this request; nothing was generated — retry in a few minutes.
data.time-budgets#Time budgets:
The model runs on CPU and one generation can take many minutes. PULSE gives each generation two clocks:
Clock Default Override Wait for the first token (queue plus prompt processing) 5 minutes PULSE_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS Decode Sized from the agent’s token budget and the platform decode rate, capped at 45 minutes PULSE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS The decode rate comes from INFERENCE_DECODE_TOK_S, which TIDE injects. If a budget is too short to produce an answer that parses, PULSE refuses up front and sends nothing to the model. The error says so and names PULSE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
data.which-model#Which model:
INFERENCE_MODEL names the model PULSE asks the server for. Set it to the general model your inference server loads — on Runink Server, a Qwen-family model under the Apache-2.0 licence. Unset, PULSE requests the same default as the shared inference library, so a locally managed child server and PULSE agree without configuration.
Every agent uses that one model. There is no second, larger tier and no per-agent model: an agent’s section in agents/pulse.ini sets its sampling parameters and its instructions, not its weights. See Model cards.
In a cluster the name is only a label — the weights actually served are pinned by the platform’s inference deployment, and PULSE is given no model name to override it.
Against a remote plane that takes the name at face value, INFERENCE_MODEL must match what that server loaded. PULSE does not check. The old LLAMA_* variable names are no longer read at all.

data:
This guide is for people changing Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine, or building against its API.
Calling the APIgrpcurl, bearer tokens, streaming, gRPC-Web, and A2A. API referenceEvery service, method, message and least role, generated from the protos.
data.architecture-in-one-paragraph#Architectu: A Go gRPC backend (grpc/) and a Flutter app (flutter/, web and Android) talk over gRPC and gRPC-Web on one port. The backend keeps its data in SQLite (one writer, so one instance), replicated by Litestream to the cluster’s object store, and its sessions and media in an appfs root on the same store. All AI is the platform’s own: the model router in front of Distro-built mistral.rs, TIDE’s ttsd for speech; no third-party model, no embeddings or RAG (product facts are read by direct corpus interaction). TIDE builds nothing here but deploys it: its pulse-operator runs the instance in pulse-system. See the Admin guide.
data.build-and-test#Build and test:
You need Go 1.26+, buf with local protoc-gen-go, protoc-gen-go-grpc and protoc-gen-dart on your PATH (remote BSR plugins silently write nothing), and Flutter 3.47.7. The backend builds only with the sibling repositories checked out next to pulse/: inference, security, mesh, store, crawler, ui, billing and ml.
# from the repository root buf generate grpc/api/proto --template grpc/buf.gen.yaml -o grpc # Go (gitignored) buf generate grpc/api/proto --template grpc/buf.gen.dart.yaml # Dart (committed), no -o cd grpc && go build ./... && go vet ./... cd grpc && TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK="$(head -c32 /dev/urandom | base64 -w0)" go test ./... cd flutter && flutter pub get && flutter analyze && flutter test The tests need TIDE_ENVELOPE_KEK because the store refuses to open without the key that seals stored credentials; any 32 random bytes, base64 encoded, will do. SQLite is pure Go, so no C toolchain is needed. After a dependency change, run sh scripts/gen-third-party-notices.sh.
Nothing in this repository needs a secret or a private tool to build or test: an outside contributor with the siblings checked out runs exactly the commands above, and CI runs the same ones.
Sibling checkouts may be on another branch. To build against a specific sibling version, add a worktree of it and point a GOWORK file outside the repository at it. Don’t switch a shared checkout. To run the backend, see Run PULSE locally.
data.how-a-change-ships#How a change ships: A merge to main triggers cd-backend.yml: it builds the pulse-backend image (backend and web app together) and rolls the one pod in pulse-system when the image digest changed. It also rebuilds every night, because the shared ui components compiled into the image are outside its path filter. The commit production runs is stamped on the live PulseControlPlane as runink.org/commit; see How a change reaches production. Cluster topology and the operator’s resource belong to TIDE: change those in TIDE, never the live Deployment.
data.pull-requests-and-ci#Pull requests and C:
Branch from origin/main and open a pull request against main; the owner squash-merges. These checks run:
Workflow Job What it checks ci.yml backend Checks out the siblings, runs buf generate, go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test -race ./... (which includes TestAPIReferenceIsCurrent) ci.yml frontend flutter analyze, flutter build web --release, and the gated flutter test with measured floors ci.yml arb keys (pull requests) grpc/tools/arbguard: fails when the pull request drops a translation key the base branch has, unless it is declared in flutter/lib/l10n/removed_keys.txt license-policy.yml licence policy Fails on stale third-party notices or a denied licence sovereignty.yml The shared blocklist of external-AI SDKs and removed dependencies, applied to every pull request gatekeeper.yml gatekeeper Lint and policy checks tide-code-review.yml, tide-agent-triage.yml, tide-agent-selfheal.yml TIDE’s review, triage and self-heal agents The review agent runs when a pull request is opened or pushed to. To ask for a review again, comment @tide_check once on the pull request (@tide_review, @core_check and @core_review are still accepted).
data.regenerate-the-api-reference#Regenerate:
The service pages of the API reference are generated from the protos and cmd/rbac_policy.go. After changing either:
cd grpc && go run ./tools/apidoc # rewrite the pages cd grpc && go run ./tools/apidoc -check # exit 1 if a page is stale Each page keeps its hand-written introduction above the generator’s marker line; everything below it is rewritten. TestAPIReferenceIsCurrent (in go test ./...) fails while a page is stale, and the generator refuses a service that no page lists or a method with no role, so a new RPC cannot ship undocumented. To place a new service, add it to pages in grpc/tools/apidoc/render.go.
data.regenerate-the-protobuf-code#Regenerate:
Run the two buf generate commands above from the repository root, and always pass the grpc/api/proto input:
The Go run needs -o grpc, or the code lands at the repository root. The Go run does not generate Dart, and nothing tells you. Skip the second and the app compiles against the old messages, and a new field reads as null on the client. The Dart output under flutter/lib/core/grpc/ is committed. Commit it with the proto change. grpc/buf.gen.go.yaml is a Go-only template for a machine with no Dart SDK. It writes into grpc itself, so run it from the repository root with the same grpc/api/proto input and no -o. Running buf from inside grpc/ picks up a competing buf.yaml and breaks import resolution. When ui changes judgement.proto, copy it again into proto-vendor/. grpc/cmd/judgement_vendored_test.go fails until you do.
data.repository-layout#Repository layout: Path What it holds grpc/ The Go backend, module github.com/org-runink/pulse (Go 1.26) grpc/main.go, grpc/cmd/ The Cobra entry point and every service. cmd/serve.go wires everything together; cmd/rbac_policy.go holds every method’s least role. grpc/api/proto/pulse/v1/ The .proto files, package pulse.v1, one or more services each grpc/api/proto-vendor/ A verbatim copy of runink/ui/judgement/v1/judgement.proto, resolved but never generated grpc/api/v1/ Generated Go code. Gitignored: run buf generate before the first build grpc/internal/ ai, db, scoring, apply, metasearch, auditdeadline, skills, skillcheck, carousel, speech, connector clients (hubspot, github, googleanalytics, googleads, …), telephony, voice, webrtc, and more grpc/agents/ Agent parameters (pulse.ini), prompt templates, and the content skills (skills///SKILL.md) grpc/data/corpus/ The product-fact files generation is grounded in, read directly by search and file read grpc/tools/ arbguard (the arb keys CI check, its own module) and apidoc (generates the API reference) flutter/lib/ The Flutter app: core/ (gRPC channel, generated stubs, theme) and features/ (one folder per screen) website/ This documentation site (Hugo + Hextra, theme vendored) The platform pieces are not here. Self-healing, the event mesh, secrets and PKI, the object store, the inference engine, the operator, and infrastructure code live in Runink TIDE or in the shared libraries. Never add them to this repository.
data.rules-for-contributions#Rules for contri:
PULSE is proprietary.
New files start with an SPDX header: SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Runink-Proprietary. Never call a third-party model or AI API, and never add embeddings or a vector index. Model output is TOON, never a JSON-schema wrapper, and the plan gate judges what a model proposes before it is saved. Nothing may publish while PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is off; a new outward channel gets its own PULSE_PUBLISH_ key. See Switches and arming order. A figure PULSE could not read is shown as not measured, never as 0. No Python and no YAML or go-toml import anywhere in the tree (tests enforce both).
