data: The site score on Brand Analysis comes from fixed, rule-based checks on your live site, not from the model. Its full report, Site Relevance Audit, is at /site-audit/report: every area, every check, and the fixes that would raise the score. The app has no menu entry for it; open it at that address.
data.apply-the-fixes-to-a-server-checkout#App:
Apply to a repo is for administrators whose site checkout lives on the PULSE server itself. Enter the repository’s path on the server, then:
Button Effect Plan Dry run: lists the file changes. Nothing is written. Apply Writes the files into that checkout. Commit Writes the changes and commits them on a branch. Copy and infrastructure changes are never applied; they come back for a person to review.
Proposing a pull request, and every button except Plan, works only for an administrator, and only when your administrator has switched on both publishing and site fixes for this PULSE. The path must be inside the directory the administrator allowed. See Switches and arming order and Site pipeline.
data.propose-a-fix-as-a-pull-request#Propose: With your website repository connected, each fix has Propose as pull request. PULSE writes that one fix on a new branch of your repository and opens a pull request for you to review and merge. PULSE never merges and never changes your base branch. The plan gate reviews the change first; if it does not agree, the fix says Withheld by the plan gate and nothing is opened. One fix gets one pull request, and the report shows its state as last read from GitHub: Pull request open, Merged, Closed without merging, or No pull request needed.
data.the-score#The score:
Your site is scored in areas such as AI visibility, search visibility, technical foundation, authority and trust, acquisition, engagement and retention, which roll up into one overall score out of 100.
Each area also reports how much of it could actually be scored. Checks that need a data source you have not connected are left out and listed under Unconfigured data sources (excluded, not zeroed), never counted as zero.
The report shows the Category breakdown, the Biggest wins, and the concrete fix-artifacts: a robots.txt, a canonical tag, a JSON-LD block, a rewritten title. Green ones are safe to apply automatically; the others need a person to review the copy or configuration.

data:
Studio (/studio) makes content and keeps what was made. It has two parts: Make something new, a list of everything Studio can make (on the left on a wide screen, folded at the top on a phone), and My Library, what was made, grouped the same way.
Making or opening a piece opens it as a card over the page, never as a page of its own; closing the card brings you back.
data.a-piece-in-my-library#A piece in My Libr:
My Library holds what was made, newest first, filed under its format’s group. A piece opens as the product itself: its words, slides, file, video or episode, its checks and its status, and what you can do with it:
Edit its words and save them back to the same piece. Approve and Schedule: the same as on the Campaigns board (see Approve and schedule). Automate: its own automation. Download: see below. Make another like this: a new card, prefilled with this piece’s title and what it was asked for. How this was made: what you asked for, when PULSE kept it. Delete: it leaves your library and will not be posted. A PDF opens with Open the PDF, a video with Watch the video, and a podcast plays in place.
data.download#Download:
Download saves an approved, scheduled or sent piece as files you can post yourself, whether the channel is connected or not:
An Instagram piece comes as one zip: the pictures (image.png for the image PULSE drew, media-01, media-02 … for your own photos, or slide-01, slide-02 … for a carousel), the video PULSE made (reel.mp4, or story-part-01.mp4 … for Stories) when it is small enough, and caption.txt with the caption and each picture’s description. A video you uploaded yourself is offered on its own, not in the zip. Any other piece comes as one text file (a Markdown file for a blog article) with its title, words, hashtags and call to action. Or each file lists the files one by one, and anything missing says why (for example an opening line too long to draw on one image).
data.instagram-pictures-and-videos#Instagram:
An Instagram piece needs your own picture or video before it can go out, except a carousel (it posts its slides):
Instagram post: Attach your photo (one photo, from upright 4:5 to wide 1.91:1). Instagram Reel: Attach your video (MP4 or MOV, 3 seconds to 15 minutes; upright 9:16 looks best). Instagram Stories: each photo or video you attach becomes one Story, in order. Instagram does not let apps add stickers (polls, questions, links): add those in the Instagram app after it is posted. PULSE checks the file against Instagram’s rules before anything is sent. Attaching publishes nothing.
A video made by PULSE. When you approve a Reel or Stories piece without a video of your own, PULSE makes one from the script: the script’s lines drawn on upright frames and read aloud by your PULSE’s speech service. The piece then says Video made from the script: N s (Stories: N parts, each with Watch part N). With no speech service, the video is made silent and says No voiceover: speech service unavailable. If a video cannot be made, the piece says why; the approval still goes through.
data.make-a-piece#Make a piece:
Pick a format. Its card shows that format’s own form and nothing else; Change format swaps it. Studio also opens from other pages with the details filled in: Create on a planned post in Campaigns, Draft on a board card.
Most social and written formats are written by a skill: PULSE writes a draft, checks it, and saves it to your Campaigns board in Drafts to approve. Nothing is posted until you approve it.
data.publishing#Publishing:
Approving a piece hands it to the schedule. Whether it goes out is decided when it is due, behind several switches, all of which must agree:
The channel is connected and switched Active in Settings → Integrations, and its card says Ready to publish. Your administrator has publishing switched on for the whole PULSE and for that channel. LinkedIn, the blog, the podcast and the audiobook also need you to be one of your PULSE’s named publishers. With Autopilot on, the post waits for the account’s best time. If one says no, the post is held back (withheld), never sent later without you, and the card says which. A channel PULSE cannot post to, or one you have not connected, says: Not connected, so PULSE will not post it. Download it and post it yourself, or connect it in Settings → Integrations.
Channel What PULSE posts Instagram Posts, carousels, Reels and Stories LinkedIn Posts, as you or as a company page you administer YouTube Shorts, uploaded to your channel Website Blog articles, to your site through GitHub Podcast and audiobook Episodes in PULSE’s own podcast feed Facebook, X, newsletters and the other formats are yours to post: download them. See Drafts, approval and publishing and, for administrators, Switches and arming order.
data.reports-and-pdfs#Reports and PDFs: Report (under Long reads and audio) writes a performance report over a period and the figures you ask it to highlight, as a PDF or a CSV. Guides, study guides, mind maps, timelines and comparison tables are made as PDFs. See Results and reports.
data.the-checks#The checks:
Under What PULSE checked, each check is a small chip: green when it passed, amber when it needs work, grey when it could not be checked (never shown as a pass). Checks depend on the format, for example Opening line, Caption, Sounds human, Slides and Hashtags. Then:
if a check failed, PULSE rewrote it once to fix what the checks found; PULSE’s reviewer (the plan gate) gives its verdict: The reviewer agreed with it, The reviewer could not check it, so it is not approved by the reviewer, or The reviewer is switched off on this server; a draft the safety rules or the reviewer refused is Not shown, with the reason. An Instagram carousel shows its slide images, drawn by PULSE, exactly as they would be posted: you approve the slides, not a description of them. Text that does not fit a slide fails its check; it is never cut. Each hashtag shows its size (posts a day: niche, medium or broad), measured from Instagram, or why it was not measured.
data.what-studio-makes#What Studio makes:
The list comes from your PULSE server, so it shows only what your PULSE can make right now. A format that cannot be made is left out, or shown with the reason (for example Video making is not installed on this PULSE yet).

data: Your website’s contact form can send each enquiry straight to Leads. Every enquiry becomes a lead in the New column, so the bell shows it as a lead waiting. When HubSpot is connected, the contact is also added to HubSpot.
data.limits#Limits: Limit Value Size of one enquiry 16 KiB (HTTP 413 above it) Per visitor address 5 at once, then 1 every 2 minutes (HTTP 429) Per link 30 at once, then 60 an hour (HTTP 429) Sites per link 10 A wrong or turned-off link answers HTTP 404. The link carries no session and no cookie: the secret in the address is the only credential, which is why it is shown once and can be replaced at any time. Turn off on the card deletes it.
data.the-snippet#The snippet:
<form method="post" action="https://pulse.example.com/inbound/leads/YOUR-SECRET"> <input name="name" placeholder="Your name" required> <input name="email" type="email" placeholder="Email" required> <input name="company" placeholder="Company"> <input name="phone" placeholder="Phone"> <textarea name="message" placeholder="How can we help?"></textarea> <input type="hidden" name="source_page" value="https://example.com/contact"> <input type="hidden" name="_redirect" value="https://example.com/thanks"> <input name="_hp" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off"> <button type="submit">Send</button> </form> The card fills in your real link.
Field Used for name, or first_name and last_name The lead’s name email The lead’s email. An email or a phone is required. company, phone Copied onto the lead message Kept in the lead’s notes, with the date source_page (or about) The lead’s source becomes website form: . For a web address, only the host and path are kept, never the query string. _redirect Where the visitor goes after sending. Only an address on one of your listed sites is followed; otherwise PULSE shows a short thank-you page. _hp or _gotcha Honeypot. A post that fills either is answered normally and stored nowhere. A script can post JSON instead (Content-Type: application/json, the same field names). It gets {"ok":true} back, or {"ok":false,"error":"…"}.
data.turn-it-on#Turn it on: Open Settings → Integrations and find the Website form card. Under Sites allowed to post, add the address of each site the form lives on, such as https://example.com. Use https://. http:// is accepted only for localhost, so you can test a page on your own computer. A browser on any other site is refused. Select Create link. The card shows the link and an HTML snippet once. Copy them now: PULSE keeps only a fingerprint (hash) of the link’s secret, so it cannot show the link again. If you lose it, select New link and update your site. The old link stops working at once.
data.what-pulse-does-with-an-enquiry#What PUL: A new email creates a lead: stage New, source website form: . An email you already have (in any letter case) adds the enquiry to that lead’s notes instead of creating a second lead. Its stage is not changed. HubSpot connected: the contact is created in HubSpot, or updated if it is already there. A HubSpot failure is logged; the lead is still saved in PULSE.
